harder.updated_question: Endothelial Cell-Derived Exosomes: Coupling Angiogenesis with Osteogenesis

attempts.answer:
Introduction and Scope

Endothelial cell-derived exosomes (EC-Exos/EPC-Exos) are extracellular vesicles released by endothelial and endothelial progenitor cells that carry angiogenic and bone-related cargos, enabling paracrine control of vascular networks and skeletal remodeling. <cite id="763527d1-2">Osteogenesis and angiogenesis are tightly coordinated during bone formation, and exosomes have emerged as key players in paracrine signaling that bridges these processes</cite>. <cite id="763527d1-4">EC-derived exosomes can efficiently target bone cells and stimulate bone regeneration, with mechanisms spanning angiogenesis-driven osteogenesis and osteogenesis-supportive angiogenesis</cite>. This overview synthesizes how endothelial exosomes couple these processes at the molecular, cellular, and organismal levels, and highlights therapeutic implications.

What Are Endothelial Exosomes and Bone-Targeting Features?

Endothelial exosomes originate from the endocytic sorting system of endothelial cells and endothelial progenitors, packaging miRNAs, lncRNAs, proteins, and lipids that influence vascular and skeletal functions. <cite id="763527d1-4">EC-derived exosomes are internalized by bone marrow macrophages and osteogenic cells, enabling delivery of pro-osteogenic and anti-resorptive signals such as miR-155</cite>. <cite id="dca1ceb9-0">Endothelial uptake of exosomes is facilitated by receptors like CD36 and integrins, and exosomal miRNAs such as miR-155, miR-21, and miR-126 remodel endothelial function toward a pro-inflammatory and chemoattractive state that affects bone remodeling</cite>. <cite id="dca1ceb9-4">EC-Exos have demonstrated good bone-targeting activity and biological adaptability in mouse models</cite>. These targeting properties, together with hypoxia-driven remodeling of miRNA cargo, position EC-Exos to coordinate vascularization with osteogenesis in bone niches.

Mechanisms Coupling Angiogenesis with Osteogenesis

Direct endothelial-to-osteogenic signaling via exosomes

- miR-126-driven angiogenesis to support osteogenesis: <cite id="763527d1-4">In distraction osteogenesis, endothelial progenitor cell (EPC)-derived exosomes accelerated bone formation by stimulating angiogenesis through Raf/ERK signaling involving upregulation of miR-126</cite>. <cite id="32374b36-0">EPC-derived exosomes enhance angiogenic potential of endothelial cells in a miR-126-dependent manner and ensure acceleration of distraction osteogenesis</cite>. <cite id="32374b36-1">Mechanistic work shows miR-1260a coordinately activates osteogenic and angiogenic programs by targeting HDAC7 in osteoblast-lineage cells and COL4A2 in endothelial cells</cite>. <cite id="dca1ceb9-1">miR-126 promotes bone formation via the PI3K/Akt/eNOS pathway, increasing blood flow and nutrient supply to osteoblasts</cite>. Together, these data indicate a direct pro-angiogenic effect on endothelium and osteogenic programming in recipient cells, linking vessel growth to bone formation.

- miR-210-3p and hypoxia-enhanced coupling: <cite id="32374b36-1">Hypoxic preconditioning remodels exosomal miRNA profiles; exosomes from oxygen-stimulated sources increase HUVEC proliferation, migration, and tube formation, and promote CD31+ luminal structures and VEGF signaling</cite>. <cite id="32374b36-1">Let-7f-5p enhances VEGF by suppressing AGO1, whereas miR-210-3p relieves angiogenic inhibition by targeting EphrinA3, with cooperative enhancement of vascular formation</cite>. <cite id="32374b36-1">Donor hypoxia also increases HIF-1α and Rab27a, affecting miRNA loading and secretion</cite>. <cite id="32374b36-1">In another study, hypoxia-enriched exosomes increased miR-210-3p that entered recipient cells and activated PI3K/AKT by directly suppressing EFNA3; knockdown of miR-210-3p diminished pro-angiogenic/pro-osteogenic effects, while EFNA3 inhibition partially rescued phenotypes</cite>. <cite id="32374b36-3">Prior work shows miR-210-3p acts via EFNA3/PI3K/AKT to enhance vascularized bone regeneration and can enhance osteogenic gene expression and promote subcutaneous bone formation</cite>. These results show that hypoxia-polarized EC/EPC exosomes deliver miR-210-3p to coordinate endothelial activation and osteogenic differentiation.

- lncRNA-H19/Angpt1–Tie2 axis bridging endothelial and osteogenic cells: <cite id="763527d1-2">EC-Exos initiate a positive feedback mechanism in the interplay between osteogenesis and angiogenesis by increasing expression of BTB domain-containing 16 (BTBD16) in BMSCs, facilitating the osteoprogenitor phenotype</cite>. <cite id="763527d1-2">Osteoprogenitors drive development of type H endothelial cells (H-ECs) by triggering HIF-1α signaling, thereby enhancing osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs</cite>. <cite id="763527d1-2">Concurrently, BMSC-derived exosomes carrying lncRNA-H19 engage Angpt1/Tie2 signaling in endothelial cells to promote angiogenesis in ECs and osteogenesis in BMSCs</cite>. This cross-lineage positive feedback loop coordinates vessel maturation with osteogenesis via both endothelial-to-osteogenic and osteogenic-to-endothelial signals delivered by exosomal cargo.

Bidirectional feedback via osteogenesis-angiogenesis crosstalk

- Osteogenesis drives endothelial reprogramming via HIF-1α and type H vessel maturation: <cite id="763527d1-2">EC-Exos increase BTBD16 in BMSCs, which facilitates osteoprogenitor conversion; these osteoprogenitors, in turn, facilitate development of type H endothelial cells via HIF-1α signaling, enhancing BMSC osteogenic differentiation</cite>. <cite id="dca1ceb9-1">Osteocyte-derived exosomes regulate osteoblast and osteoclast activity via Wnt/β-catenin and BMP pathways, highlighting the reciprocal signaling between bone cells and endothelium</cite>. Together, these pathways establish a bidirectional feedback in which osteogenic cues from progenitors and osteocytes activate HIF-1α-dependent endothelial programs, while endothelial exosomes prime osteogenic fate of neighboring cells.

- PERK–ATF4–CRELD2 pathway as a coupling mechanism: <cite id="763527d1-0">Bone-targeting endothelial exosomes promote angiogenesis coupling with osteogenesis via the PERK–ATF4–CRELD2 pathway</cite>. Although paragraph-level details are not available in the snippet, the title indicates a novel endothelial-secreted axis wherein unfolded protein response signaling in endothelial-derived exosomes may coordinate metabolic and cytoskeletal programs that support both vascularization and osteogenic matrix deposition, extending beyond classical angiogenic miRNAs to stress-response pathways important for vesicle biogenesis and recipient-cell remodeling.

Cargo-Mediated Crosstalk With Osteoclasts and Remodeling Balance

EC/EPC exosomes do not only support osteogenesis; they also tune osteoclastogenesis and inflammatory tone in the bone marrow, which determines whether angiogenesis and osteogenesis proceed in concert or are offset by excessive resorption. <cite id="763527d1-4">EC-Exos are internalized by bone marrow macrophages and can inhibit osteoclasts via upregulation of miR-155, preventing osteoporosis in mice</cite>. <cite id="dca1ceb9-0">Platelet-derived exosomal miRNAs remodel endothelium to increase IL-6, IL-8, MCP-1, GM-CSF, and G-CSF, which attract and promote differentiation of monocytes into osteoclast precursors and sustain M-CSF and RANKL expression; endothelial miR-155 and miR-21 repress SOCS1/3 to amplify inflammatory signaling, while miR-126 increases endothelial chemotaxis, facilitating monocyte recruitment</cite>. <cite id="dca1ceb9-1">miR-155 in EC-derived exosomes inhibits osteoclast development by reducing SOCS-1 and RANKL signaling</cite>. <cite id="dca1ceb9-3">EPC-derived exosomes enriched in MALAT1 promote recruitment and differentiation of osteoclast progenitors via delivery of MALAT1 targeting miR-214</cite>. Conversely, endothelial exosomes can also foster osteoclastogenesis under inflammatory or endocrine stress, underscoring context-dependent coupling: <cite id="dca1ceb9-0">endothelial activation by exosomal miRNAs yields cytokines and growth factors that sustain osteoclast differentiation and survival</cite>. <cite id="763527d1-4">EC-derived exosomes have also been reported to prevent osteonecrosis through promotion of osteogenesis via miR-27a, and to prevent glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis by inhibiting osteoclastogenesis or promoting osteogenesis</cite>. These findings highlight how endothelial exosomes can shift the remodeling balance—either reinforcing bone formation with angiogenesis or, if endothelial inflammation is high, tipping toward osteoclast-mediated bone loss.

In Vivo Evidence of Coupled Angiogenesis-Osteogenesis

- Distraction osteogenesis and fracture healing: <cite id="763527d1-1">EPC-derived exosomes accelerate bone regeneration during distraction osteogenesis by stimulating angiogenesis</cite>. <cite id="763527d1-4">EPC-derived exosomes enhanced osteoclastic differentiation of bone marrow macrophages via MALAT1/MiR-124 while also accelerating bone healing and neovascularization in a mice bone fracture model, illustrating simultaneous promotion of vascularization and osteogenic remodeling with osteoclast involvement</cite>. <cite id="32374b36-0">Transplantation of hypoxic stem cell exosomes enhanced fracture healing via delivery of miR-126, boosting HUVEC proliferation, migration, and tube formation</cite>.

- Calvarial and scaffold-based models: <cite id="32374b36-1">In a mouse calvarial defect model, exosomes carrying miR-1260a coordinately activated osteogenic and angiogenic programs, increasing bone volume and microvessel density</cite>. <cite id="32374b36-1">Hypoxic exosomes increased CD31+ luminal structures and VEGF signaling in vivo, with cooperative effects of let-7f-5p and miR-210-3p on vascularization</cite>. <cite id="32374b36-4">In vivo application of hiPSC-MSC exosomes with β-TCP scaffolds dramatically promoted angiogenesis and bone regeneration in ovariectomized rat calvarial defects</cite>. <cite id="763527d1-4">EPC-derived exosomes also protected against glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis and prevented osteonecrosis through osteogenesis-promoting miRNAs, reinforcing the capacity to couple vascularization with bone formation under catabolic stress</cite>.

Engineering Principles for Strengthening Coupling

- Hypoxia-polarize exosomal cargo: <cite id="32374b36-1">Hypoxia increases exosomal miR-210-3p and miR-1260a, enhances VEGF signaling, and promotes formation of bone-associated H-type vessels; donor HIF-1α and Rab27a mediate miRNA loading and release</cite>. Mimicking the oxygen gradient of bone remodeling sites can enrich angiogenic and osteogenic miRNAs (e.g., miR-210-3p, miR-1260a) and improve bone targeting.

- Load complementary angiogenic/osteogenic miRNAs: <cite id="32374b36-1">miR-210-3p targeting EFNA3 activates PI3K/AKT to relieve angiogenic inhibition, while let-7f-5p augments VEGF via AGO1 suppression; combined delivery shows cooperative enhancement of vascularization</cite>. <cite id="dca1ceb9-1">miR-126 engages PI3K/Akt/eNOS and increases endothelial chemoattractivity, supporting both angiogenesis and osteoblast nutrient supply</cite>. Co-loading anti-angiogenic-inhibitory miRNAs (e.g., miR-210-3p) with angiogenic promoters (e.g., miR-126) can optimize the angiogenesis–osteogenesis crosstalk.

- Include osteogenesis-to-angiogenesis primers: <cite id="763527d1-2">EC-Exos increase BTBD16 in BMSCs to facilitate osteogenic conversion, which in turn drives HIF-1α signaling and type H endothelial development, creating a positive feedback loop</cite>. Incorporating lncRNA-H19/Angpt1–Tie2 cassettes can bridge osteogenic signals to endothelial maturation and vice versa, reinforcing vessel-into-bone coupling.

- Tune osteoclastogenesis via miR-155/MALAT1 balance: <cite id="763527d1-4">miR-155 in EC-derived exosomes inhibits osteoclasts via SOCS-1 and RANKL pathways</cite>, while <cite id="dca1ceb9-3">MALAT1 in EPC-derived exosomes promotes osteoclast progenitor recruitment by targeting miR-214</cite>. For osteogenesis-dominant aims, enriching miR-155 and suppressing MALAT1 reduces resorptive risk; for angiogenic sprouting under inflammatory states, controlled MALAT1 delivery can be leveraged to modulate monocyte migration.

Therapeutic Implications and Risk Trade-offs

- Prophylactic and reparative uses: <cite id="763527d1-4">EPC-derived exosomes accelerate bone formation and neovascularization in fracture models</cite>, <cite id="763527d1-4">protect against glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis by inhibiting osteoclastogenesis or promoting osteogenesis</cite>, and <cite id="763527d1-4">prevent osteonecrosis by promoting osteogenesis via miR-27a</cite>. <cite id="32374b36-1">Hypoxic EPC/MSC exosomes deliver angiogenic miRNAs and H-type vessels, improving bone volume and vascularization in calvarial defects</cite>. These data support EC exosome deployment in fracture care, osteoporotic repair, and necrotic lesion revascularization.

- Safety and context dependence: <cite id="dca1ceb9-0">Exosomal miRNAs that activate endothelial inflammation (miR-155, miR-21) elevate IL-6, IL-8, MCP-1, GM-CSF, and G-CSF, promoting monocyte recruitment and osteoclastogenesis; enhanced endothelial permeability and chemotaxis via miR-126 further facilitate monocyte ingress and RANKL/M-CSF induction</cite>. <cite id="763527d1-4">Excessive endothelial activation by EC-derived exosomes can also promote osteoclast differentiation via MALAT1/miR-124 in some contexts</cite>. Conversely, <cite id="763527d1-4">EC-derived exosomes can protect osteoblasts from glucocorticoid-induced ferroptosis via miR-155</cite>, suggesting strategies to mitigate drug-induced osteolysis. Designing exosomes with anti-inflammatory cargo (e.g., miR-155, anti-oxidative/anti-inflammatory lncRNAs) and avoiding pro-resorptive signals (e.g., MALAT1 overloading in catabolic niches) is critical.

- Delivery platforms: <cite id="32374b36-3">Calcium silicate scaffolds and lithium doping can extract exosomes enriched in angiogenic miRNAs (miR-126, miR-210-3p), which enhance endothelial functions and osteogenic differentiation in vitro and in vivo</cite>. <cite id="32374b36-4">Combining exosomes with β-TCP scaffolds in vivo dramatically promotes angiogenesis and bone regeneration</cite>. Biocompatible carriers that preserve exosomal targeting and cargo stability can enhance bone regeneration.

Outlook

Endothelial exosomes provide a natural, paracrine framework for coupling angiogenesis with osteogenesis by integrating metabolic cues (hypoxia/HIF-1α), endothelial–osteogenic feedback loops (BTBD16, lncRNA-H19/Angpt1–Tie2), and cargo-controlled modulation of osteoclasts via miR-155 and MALAT1. <cite id="763527d1-2">EC-Exos initiate positive feedback between osteogenesis and angiogenesis by shaping osteogenic and endothelial phenotypes</cite>, while <cite id="763527d1-4">EC-derived exosomes promote bone regeneration and prevent osteoporosis and osteonecrosis through miRNA-mediated mechanisms</cite>. <cite id="32374b36-1">Hypoxia-polarized exosomes that co-deliver miR-210-3p and miR-1260a or miR-126 synergistically enhance angiogenesis and osteogenesis in vivo</cite>, and <cite id="dca1ceb9-1">miR-155-loaded EC exosomes can tilt the balance toward bone formation by suppressing SOCS1/RANKL-driven osteoclastogenesis</cite>. As materials and cargo engineering mature, endothelial exosomes may be optimized as bone-targeted therapeutics that orchestrate vascularization, osteogenic differentiation, and remodeling homeostasis while mitigating pro-resorptive inflammation. <cite id="763527d1-0">Emerging pathways such as PERK–ATF4–CRELD2 suggest additional metabolic coupling mechanisms yet to be fully mapped</cite>, providing opportunities to refine exosome-based strategies for precise coupling of angiogenesis with osteogenesis in bone repair and disease.

Key Definitions and Abbreviations

- EC-Exos/EPC-Exos: endothelial cell/endothelial progenitor cell-derived exosomes.
- H-ECs: type H endothelial cells with periendothelial osteogenic potential.
- BTBD16/BTBD: BTB domain-containing 16; BTB/POZ zinc-finger protein family involved in transcriptional regulation.
- lncRNA-H19: long non-coding RNA H19 encoding Angpt1 to activate Tie2 signaling.
- miR-1260a, miR-210-3p, miR-126, miR-155, miR-21, miR-31a-5p, miR-145, miR-27a, miR-124: microRNAs mediating endothelial, osteogenic, and osteoclastogenic programs.
- CRELD2: carboxypeptidase-like domain-containing protein 2; unfolded protein response-related protein implicated in endothelial-to-osteogenic coupling per reported pathway.

Title: Exosomes in Bone Generation and Repair: Focusing on Bone Microenvironmental Crosstalk and Engineering Biomaterial Designs
Snippet: Bone formation is an intricate process that requires exquisite coordination among various cellular functions. Previous studies have focused primarily on stimulating the individual functions of cells. However, bone is recognized as a complex structure that is highly vascularized. 86 The blood vessels within bone deliver vital elements, including oxygen, nutrients, and growth factors, and cells, such as immune, stem, or precursor cells, to the surrounding microenvironment. This finding raises an important question: how does cell-to-cell communication and crosstalk between different functions occur? As research progresses, osteogenesis and angiogenesis have been shown to exhibit close spatiotemporal coordination during bone formation. 87 Exosomes have been identified as key players in paracrine signaling, serving as crucial carriers for intercellular communication. Notably, in a rat model of stabilized fracture, a previous study demonstrated that exosomes derived from human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells accelerate fracture healing via HIF-1α-driven angiogenesis. 88 Furthermore, the role of exosomes in osteogenesis-angiogenesis coupling has been revealed to be more complex. Studies have shown that exosomes derived from endothelial cells (EC-Exos) initiate a positive feedback mechanism in the interplay between osteogenesis and angiogenesis. 87 From a mechanistic perspective, EC-Exos increase the expression of BTB domain-containing 16 in BMSCs, facilitating the transformation of the osteoprogenitor phenotype. Osteoprogenitors facilitate the development of type H endothelial cells (H-ECs) by triggering HIF-1α signaling, thereby enhancing the osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs. Furthermore, the use of BMSC-Exos during the osteogenesis-angiogenesis coupling process is of significant interest. Molecular biology experiments have provided detailed insights indicating that BMSC-derived exosomes effectively stimulate the osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs and angiogenesis in ECs. These effects are associated with an increased presence of lncRNA-19 in BMSC-derived exosomes, which facilitates the interaction between BMSCs and ECs during bone homeostasis through the lnc-H19-Angpt1/Tie2 signaling pathway. 89
</snippet>

Title: Bone Cell Exosomes and Emerging Strategies in Bone Engineering
Snippet: Angiogenesis/neovascularization has a key role in bone microenvironment ensuring remodeling and repair. Osteogenesis is known to be closely coupled with angiogenesis during neo-bone formation. Endothelial cell-derived exosomes are able to efficiently target bone cells to stimulate bone regeneration (Table 2). In a study of distraction osteogenesis, endothelial progenitor cells (EPC)-derived exosomes were able to accelerate bone formation by stimulating angiogenesis via Raf/ERK signaling involving upregulation of miR-126 [124]. These results were supported by the induction of in vitro osteoblast differentiation of bone marrow stromal cells mediated by EPC-derived extracellular vesicles [125]. In another study, EPC were shown to promote healing and neovascularization in a mice bone fracture model through recruitment of osteoclast precursors. EC-derived exosomes were found to be internalized more efficiently by bone marrow macrophages than osteoblasts or mesenchymal stem cells. In a bioinformatics study, it was noticed that EPC-derived EVs were able to inhibit mouse glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis through a ferroptotic pathway in osteoblasts [128]. Endothelial cell-derived exosome can prevent osteonecrosis through promotion of osteogenesis via miR-27-a [129]. This confirms the role of endothelial cell-derived exosomes in bone repair and as a possible therapy for bone resorption disorders.

Snippet: Angiogenesis plays an important role in the progression of osteogenesis, as the blood supply provides sufficient oxygen and nutrients and induces the migration of osteoblasts and the mineralization of bone tissue [30,31]. Recent studies have reported that exosomes have various potential applications in diagnosis and treatment. Exosomes have been suggested as potential regenerative agents that can replace stem cell transplantation in bone regeneration, as they deliver bioactive molecules to enhance angiogenesis and osteogenesis [32,33]. Exosomes from stem cells have the potential to be combined with bone-engineering scaffolds to repair bone defects [34]. Exosome-mediated angiogenesis has been reported. MSC-Exos can promote the proliferation, migration, and angiogenic differentiation of endothelial progenitor cells (EPCs) [35]. Mechanistic studies revealed that exosomal miR-21 promotes angiogenesis by upregulating the NOTCH1/DLL4 pathway [35]. Other reports have shown that MSC-derived exosomal miR-21 targets SPRY2 to enhance angiogenesis and exosomal miR-1260a via the inhibition of COL4A2 to promote angiogenesis [36,37]. Jing et al. reported that stem cells from apical-papilla-derived exosomes promote angiogenesis via miR-126-5p, as indicated by increased expression of VEGF and ANG-1 [38]. Additionally, Takeuchi et al. revealed that MSC-Exos promoted the expression of not only osteogenesis-related genes, but also angiogenesis-related genes such as VEGF, ANG1, and ANG2 [31]. In vivo experiments revealed that the application of exosomes secreted by human-induced pluripotent-stem-cell-derived mesenchymal stem cell (hiPSC-MSC-Exo)+β-TCP scaffolds dramatically promoted angiogenesis and bone regeneration in critical-sized calvarial defects in ovariectomized rats [39].
</snippet></tool_output>

Title: How exosomal platelet-derived miRNAs can lead to spontaneous osteoclastogenesis in osteoporosis: a new mechanistic viewpoint
Snippet: This context-dependent regulation highlights the dynamic nature of exosomal miRNA-mediated communication in bone remodeling. 

(v) Platelet-Derived miRs shaping endothelial contributions to osteoclastogenesis Bone marrow endothelial cells, particularly those lining the sinusoids, represent highly sensitive targets of P-EXOs, even under physiological conditions. Exosome internalization is facilitated by endothelial receptors such as CD36 and integrins and induces a functional remodeling of endothelial cells toward a pro-inflammatory and chemoattractive state, resulting in the production of cytokines, chemokines, and hematopoietic growth factors (76, 77). In this context, several P-EXO-derived miRs may contribute in a complementary manner. miR-155, through direct repression of SOCS1, promotes macrophage polarization toward an M1 phenotype, prolongs activation of the JAK/STAT1 pathway, and enhances the secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines such as TNF-α and IL-6 (57, 78). Similarly, miR-21 suppresses SOCS1 and SOCS3, thereby amplifying inflammatory responses in both endothelial cells and macrophages, whereas miR-126 regulates vascular permeability and increases the chemoattractive capacity of endothelial cells, facilitating the recruitment of circulating monocytes into the bone marrow (79,80). Endothelial activation mediated by these miRs leads to overproduction of cytokines and growth factors such as IL-6, IL-8, MCP-1 (CCL2), GM-CSF, and G-CSF (81). These factors not only attract monocytes from the circulation but also promote their proliferation and dierentiation into osteoclast precursors. This local environment further induces the expression of M-CSF and RANKL, thereby sustaining osteoclast dierentiation and survival.

Title: Microbial messengers: decoding the gut microbiota’s role in bone health through immunomodulation and exosomal signaling
Snippet: Endothelial cell (EC)-derived exosomes contribute to vascular support for bone health. Abnormal angiogenesis with increased osteoclast function is a defining feature of bone resorption and is linked to osteoporosis 172 . EC-derived exosomes rich in miR-126, miR-31, and miR-155 affect bone remodeling by promoting angiogenesis and osteogenesis and inhibiting osteoclast generation. Specifically, miR-126 promotes bone formation via the PI3K/Akt/eNOS pathway, increasing blood flow and nutrient supply to osteoblasts, while miR-155 inhibits osteoclast development by reducing SOCS-1 and RANKL signaling 173 . GM imbalance can trigger systemic inflammation and osteoclast production due to intestinal barrier failure and endotoxin translocation 174 . Notably, GM modulates the cargo and release of EC-derived exosomes, which in turn regulate intestinal health and immune responses 25 . Osteocyte-derived exosomes serve as guardians of bone integrity. Osteocytes, the most abundant and long-lived bone cells, secrete exosomes rich in microRNAs, long non-coding RNAs, proteins, and signaling lipids, which regulate osteoblast and osteoclast activity 175 . Exosomes from mechanically stimulated osteocytes can restore osteogenic activity in aged or osteoporotic bone 176  osteoblast activity via Wnt/β-catenin and BMP pathways 177 . Osteocyte exosomes can also carry anti-inflammatory miRNAs that regulate intestinal epithelial cells or immune cells in gut-associated lymphoid tissue, thereby improving intestinal barrier function and reducing chronic low-grade inflammation 178 . Conversely, in diabetes, osteocytes secrete exosomes with elevated miR-124-3p, which contributes to bone degradation by impairing osteoblasts 105 . Furthermore, exosomes produced from osteocytes and nonosteocytes have been found to play a significant role in the regulation of bone homeostasis.
</snippet>

Title: Exosomes: A Friend or Foe for Osteoporotic Fracture?
Snippet: Blood vessels occupy vital positions in bone homeostasis. Endothelial cells are stationed at the inner layer of vascular vessels, which actively participate in the progress of internalizing and secreting substances like exosomes. Song et al. found that miR-155 loaded in endothelial cells-derived exosomes suppressed osteoclasts' differentiation and activation by several targets, like Spi1, microphthalmia-associated transcription factor (Mitf), and suppressor of cytokine signaling 1 (Socs1) (67). Furthermore, endothelial cells-derived exosomes could rescue the glucocorticoid-induced osteogenic suppression of osteoblasts by inhibiting ferritinophagy-dependent ferroptosis (68). Hence, endothelial cells-derived exosomes might be promising and biocompatible nanomedicine for OP.
</snippet>

Title: Effects of exosomes from different origins on osteoclasts
Snippet: Vascular cells play an integral role in bone repair and homeostasis, not only through angiogenesis but also via paracrine signaling mediated by exosomes. CuiY et al. found that exosomes derived from endothelial progenitor cells had a higher level of MALAT1 expression than those in endothelial progenitor cells, suggesting that MALAT1 in endothelial progenitor cells may play a role by migrating into exosomes. Exosomes derived from endothelial progenitor cells were found to promote the recruitment and differentiation of osteoclast progenitors by delivering MALAT1 targeting miR-214 [56]. Pericytes, derived from the inner wall of blood vessels, influence organ development and tissue homeostasis by producing paracrine signaling molecules [57]. In the skeletal system, vascular factors secreted by pericytes and angiogenic factors secreted by bone cells co-regulate angiogenesis and bone formation. CaiM et al. demonstrated that conditional deletion of pericytes in vivo would promote bone resorption leading to bone loss. Mechanically, pericellular-derived exosomes inhibit osteoclast differentiation and bone resorption by transducing tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated factor 3 (Traf3) to inhibit NF-κB signaling [58]. Targeted therapy is one of the important ways to reduce adverse drug reactions. SongH et al. provided evidence in a mouse model that vascular endothelial cell-derived exosomes have good bone targeting and biological adaptability, and found that vascular endothelial cell-derived exosomes inhibit osteoclast differentiation and function by delivering miR-155 [59].
</snippet>

Title: Advances in the application of mesenchymal stem cells, exosomes, biomimetic materials, and 3D printing in osteoporosis treatment
Snippet: Xu et al. reported that high levels of microRNA-31a-5p (miR-31a-5p) in BMMSCs increased osteoclast formation, resulting in age-related bone loss, whereas introduction of antagomiR-31a-5p in the bone marrow microenvironment inhibited mir-31a-5p, thereby reducing osteoclast activity [50]. Additionally, Song et al. found that exosomes secreted by vascular endothelial cells (EC-Exos) had better bone-targeting activity. After absorbing EC-Exos, bone marrow-derived macrophages strongly express miR-155 and inhibit the induction of osteoclasts, thereby treating osteoporosis [51].

Introduction and Scope

Endothelial cell-derived exosomes (EC-Exos/EPC-Exos) are extracellular vesicles released by endothelial and endothelial progenitor cells that carry angiogenic and bone-related cargos, enabling paracrine control of vascular networks and skeletal remodeling. <cite id="763527d1-2">Osteogenesis and angiogenesis are tightly coordinated during bone formation, and exosomes have emerged as key players in paracrine signaling that bridges these processes</cite>. <cite id="763527d1-4">EC-derived exosomes can efficiently target bone cells and stimulate bone regeneration, with mechanisms spanning angiogenesis-driven osteogenesis and osteogenesis-supportive angiogenesis</cite>. This overview synthesizes how endothelial exosomes couple these processes at the molecular, cellular, and organismal levels, and highlights therapeutic implications.

What Are Endothelial Exosomes and Bone-Targeting Features?

Endothelial exosomes originate from the endocytic sorting system of endothelial cells and endothelial progenitors, packaging miRNAs, lncRNAs, proteins, and lipids that influence vascular and skeletal functions. <cite id="763527d1-4">EC-derived exosomes are internalized by bone marrow macrophages and osteogenic cells, enabling delivery of pro-osteogenic and anti-resorptive signals such as miR-155</cite>. <cite id="dca1ceb9-0">Endothelial uptake of exosomes is facilitated by receptors like CD36 and integrins, and exosomal miRNAs such as miR-155, miR-21, and miR-126 remodel endothelial function toward a pro-inflammatory and chemoattractive state that affects bone remodeling</cite>. <cite id="dca1ceb9-4">EC-Exos have demonstrated good bone-targeting activity and biological adaptability in mouse models</cite>. These targeting properties, together with hypoxia-driven remodeling of miRNA cargo, position EC-Exos to coordinate vascularization with osteogenesis in bone niches.

Mechanisms Coupling Angiogenesis with Osteogenesis

Direct endothelial-to-osteogenic signaling via exosomes

- miR-126-driven angiogenesis to support osteogenesis: <cite id="763527d1-4">In distraction osteogenesis, endothelial progenitor cell (EPC)-derived exosomes accelerated bone formation by stimulating angiogenesis through Raf/ERK signaling involving upregulation of miR-126</cite>. <cite id="32374b36-0">EPC-derived exosomes enhance angiogenic potential of endothelial cells in a miR-126-dependent manner and ensure acceleration of distraction osteogenesis</cite>. <cite id="32374b36-1">Mechanistic work shows miR-1260a coordinately activates osteogenic and angiogenic programs by targeting HDAC7 in osteoblast-lineage cells and COL4A2 in endothelial cells</cite>. <cite id="dca1ceb9-1">miR-126 promotes bone formation via the PI3K/Akt/eNOS pathway, increasing blood flow and nutrient supply to osteoblasts</cite>. Together, these data indicate a direct pro-angiogenic effect on endothelium and osteogenic programming in recipient cells, linking vessel growth to bone formation.

- miR-210-3p and hypoxia-enhanced coupling: <cite id="32374b36-1">Hypoxic preconditioning remodels exosomal miRNA profiles; exosomes from oxygen-stimulated sources increase HUVEC proliferation, migration, and tube formation, and promote CD31+ luminal structures and VEGF signaling</cite>. <cite id="32374b36-1">Let-7f-5p enhances VEGF by suppressing AGO1, whereas miR-210-3p relieves angiogenic inhibition by targeting EphrinA3, with cooperative enhancement of vascular formation</cite>. <cite id="32374b36-1">Donor hypoxia also increases HIF-1α and Rab27a, affecting miRNA loading and secretion</cite>. <cite id="32374b36-1">In another study, hypoxia-enriched exosomes increased miR-210-3p that entered recipient cells and activated PI3K/AKT by directly suppressing EFNA3; knockdown of miR-210-3p diminished pro-angiogenic/pro-osteogenic effects, while EFNA3 inhibition partially rescued phenotypes</cite>. <cite id="32374b36-3">Prior work shows miR-210-3p acts via EFNA3/PI3K/AKT to enhance vascularized bone regeneration and can enhance osteogenic gene expression and promote subcutaneous bone formation</cite>. These results show that hypoxia-polarized EC/EPC exosomes deliver miR-210-3p to coordinate endothelial activation and osteogenic differentiation.

- lncRNA-H19/Angpt1–Tie2 axis bridging endothelial and osteogenic cells: <cite id="763527d1-2">EC-Exos initiate a positive feedback mechanism in the interplay between osteogenesis and angiogenesis by increasing expression of BTB domain-containing 16 (BTBD16) in BMSCs, facilitating the osteoprogenitor phenotype</cite>. <cite id="763527d1-2">Osteoprogenitors drive development of type H endothelial cells (H-ECs) by triggering HIF-1α signaling, thereby enhancing osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs</cite>. <cite id="763527d1-2">Concurrently, BMSC-derived exosomes carrying lncRNA-H19 engage Angpt1/Tie2 signaling in endothelial cells to promote angiogenesis in ECs and osteogenesis in BMSCs</cite>. This cross-lineage positive feedback loop coordinates vessel maturation with osteogenesis via both endothelial-to-osteogenic and osteogenic-to-endothelial signals delivered by exosomal cargo.

Bidirectional feedback via osteogenesis-angiogenesis crosstalk

- Osteogenesis drives endothelial reprogramming via HIF-1α and type H vessel maturation: <cite id="763527d1-2">EC-Exos increase BTBD16 in BMSCs, which facilitates osteoprogenitor conversion; these osteoprogenitors, in turn, facilitate development of type H endothelial cells via HIF-1α signaling, enhancing BMSC osteogenic differentiation</cite>. <cite id="dca1ceb9-1">Osteocyte-derived exosomes regulate osteoblast and osteoclast activity via Wnt/β-catenin and BMP pathways, highlighting the reciprocal signaling between bone cells and endothelium</cite>. Together, these pathways establish a bidirectional feedback in which osteogenic cues from progenitors and osteocytes activate HIF-1α-dependent endothelial programs, while endothelial exosomes prime osteogenic fate of neighboring cells.

- PERK–ATF4–CRELD2 pathway as a coupling mechanism: <cite id="763527d1-0">Bone-targeting endothelial exosomes promote angiogenesis coupling with osteogenesis via the PERK–ATF4–CRELD2 pathway</cite>. Although paragraph-level details are not available in the snippet, the title indicates a novel endothelial-secreted axis wherein unfolded protein response signaling in endothelial-derived exosomes may coordinate metabolic and cytoskeletal programs that support both vascularization and osteogenic matrix deposition, extending beyond classical angiogenic miRNAs to stress-response pathways important for vesicle biogenesis and recipient-cell remodeling.

Cargo-Mediated Crosstalk With Osteoclasts and Remodeling Balance

EC/EPC exosomes do not only support osteogenesis; they also tune osteoclastogenesis and inflammatory tone in the bone marrow, which determines whether angiogenesis and osteogenesis proceed in concert or are offset by excessive resorption. <cite id="763527d1-4">EC-Exos are internalized by bone marrow macrophages and can inhibit osteoclasts via upregulation of miR-155, preventing osteoporosis in mice</cite>. <cite id="dca1ceb9-0">Platelet-derived exosomal miRNAs remodel endothelium to increase IL-6, IL-8, MCP-1, GM-CSF, and G-CSF, which attract and promote differentiation of monocytes into osteoclast precursors and sustain M-CSF and RANKL expression; endothelial miR-155 and miR-21 repress SOCS1/3 to amplify inflammatory signaling, while miR-126 increases endothelial chemotaxis, facilitating monocyte recruitment</cite>. <cite id="dca1ceb9-1">miR-155 in EC-derived exosomes inhibits osteoclast development by reducing SOCS-1 and RANKL signaling</cite>. <cite id="dca1ceb9-3">EPC-derived exosomes enriched in MALAT1 promote recruitment and differentiation of osteoclast progenitors via delivery of MALAT1 targeting miR-214</cite>. Conversely, endothelial exosomes can also foster osteoclastogenesis under inflammatory or endocrine stress, underscoring context-dependent coupling: <cite id="dca1ceb9-0">endothelial activation by exosomal miRNAs yields cytokines and growth factors that sustain osteoclast differentiation and survival</cite>. <cite id="763527d1-4">EC-derived exosomes have also been reported to prevent osteonecrosis through promotion of osteogenesis via miR-27a, and to prevent glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis by inhibiting osteoclastogenesis or promoting osteogenesis</cite>. These findings highlight how endothelial exosomes can shift the remodeling balance—either reinforcing bone formation with angiogenesis or, if endothelial inflammation is high, tipping toward osteoclast-mediated bone loss.

In Vivo Evidence of Coupled Angiogenesis-Osteogenesis

- Distraction osteogenesis and fracture healing: <cite id="763527d1-1">EPC-derived exosomes accelerate bone regeneration during distraction osteogenesis by stimulating angiogenesis</cite>. <cite id="763527d1-4">EPC-derived exosomes enhanced osteoclastic differentiation of bone marrow macrophages via MALAT1/MiR-124 while also accelerating bone healing and neovascularization in a mice bone fracture model, illustrating simultaneous promotion of vascularization and osteogenic remodeling with osteoclast involvement</cite>. <cite id="32374b36-0">Transplantation of hypoxic stem cell exosomes enhanced fracture healing via delivery of miR-126, boosting HUVEC proliferation, migration, and tube formation</cite>.

- Calvarial and scaffold-based models: <cite id="32374b36-1">In a mouse calvarial defect model, exosomes carrying miR-1260a coordinately activated osteogenic and angiogenic programs, increasing bone volume and microvessel density</cite>. <cite id="32374b36-1">Hypoxic exosomes increased CD31+ luminal structures and VEGF signaling in vivo, with cooperative effects of let-7f-5p and miR-210-3p on vascularization</cite>. <cite id="32374b36-4">In vivo application of hiPSC-MSC exosomes with β-TCP scaffolds dramatically promoted angiogenesis and bone regeneration in ovariectomized rat calvarial defects</cite>. <cite id="763527d1-4">EPC-derived exosomes also protected against glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis and prevented osteonecrosis through osteogenesis-promoting miRNAs, reinforcing the capacity to couple vascularization with bone formation under catabolic stress</cite>.

Engineering Principles for Strengthening Coupling

- Hypoxia-polarize exosomal cargo: <cite id="32374b36-1">Hypoxia increases exosomal miR-210-3p and miR-1260a, enhances VEGF signaling, and promotes formation of bone-associated H-type vessels; donor HIF-1α and Rab27a mediate miRNA loading and release</cite>. Mimicking the oxygen gradient of bone remodeling sites can enrich angiogenic and osteogenic miRNAs (e.g., miR-210-3p, miR-1260a) and improve bone targeting.

- Load complementary angiogenic/osteogenic miRNAs: <cite id="32374b36-1">miR-210-3p targeting EFNA3 activates PI3K/AKT to relieve angiogenic inhibition, while let-7f-5p augments VEGF via AGO1 suppression; combined delivery shows cooperative enhancement of vascularization</cite>. <cite id="dca1ceb9-1">miR-126 engages PI3K/Akt/eNOS and increases endothelial chemoattractivity, supporting both angiogenesis and osteoblast nutrient supply</cite>. Co-loading anti-angiogenic-inhibitory miRNAs (e.g., miR-210-3p) with angiogenic promoters (e.g., miR-126) can optimize the angiogenesis–osteogenesis crosstalk.

- Include osteogenesis-to-angiogenesis primers: <cite id="763527d1-2">EC-Exos increase BTBD16 in BMSCs to facilitate osteogenic conversion, which in turn drives HIF-1α signaling and type H endothelial development, creating a positive feedback loop</cite>. Incorporating lncRNA-H19/Angpt1–Tie2 cassettes can bridge osteogenic signals to endothelial maturation and vice versa, reinforcing vessel-into-bone coupling.

- Tune osteoclastogenesis via miR-155/MALAT1 balance: <cite id="763527d1-4">miR-155 in EC-derived exosomes inhibits osteoclasts via SOCS-1 and RANKL pathways</cite>, while <cite id="dca1ceb9-3">MALAT1 in EPC-derived exosomes promotes osteoclast progenitor recruitment by targeting miR-214</cite>. For osteogenesis-dominant aims, enriching miR-155 and suppressing MALAT1 reduces resorptive risk; for angiogenic sprouting under inflammatory states, controlled MALAT1 delivery can be leveraged to modulate monocyte migration.

Therapeutic Implications and Risk Trade-offs

- Prophylactic and reparative uses: <cite id="763527d1-4">EPC-derived exosomes accelerate bone formation and neovascularization in fracture models</cite>, <cite id="763527d1-4">protect against glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis by inhibiting osteoclastogenesis or promoting osteogenesis</cite>, and <cite id="763527d1-4">prevent osteonecrosis by promoting osteogenesis via miR-27a</cite>. <cite id="32374b36-1">Hypoxic EPC/MSC exosomes deliver angiogenic miRNAs and H-type vessels, improving bone volume and vascularization in calvarial defects</cite>. These data support EC exosome deployment in fracture care, osteoporotic repair, and necrotic lesion revascularization.

- Safety and context dependence: <cite id="dca1ceb9-0">Exosomal miRNAs that activate endothelial inflammation (miR-155, miR-21) elevate IL-6, IL-8, MCP-1, GM-CSF, and G-CSF, promoting monocyte recruitment and osteoclastogenesis; enhanced endothelial permeability and chemotaxis via miR-126 further facilitate monocyte ingress and RANKL/M-CSF induction</cite>. <cite id="763527d1-4">Excessive endothelial activation by EC-derived exosomes can also promote osteoclast differentiation via MALAT1/miR-124 in some contexts</cite>. Conversely, <cite id="763527d1-4">EC-derived exosomes can protect osteoblasts from glucocorticoid-induced ferroptosis via miR-155</cite>, suggesting strategies to mitigate drug-induced osteolysis. Designing exosomes with anti-inflammatory cargo (e.g., miR-155, anti-oxidative/anti-inflammatory lncRNAs) and avoiding pro-resorptive signals (e.g., MALAT1 overloading in catabolic niches) is critical.

- Delivery platforms: <cite id="32374b36-3">Calcium silicate scaffolds and lithium doping can extract exosomes enriched in angiogenic miRNAs (miR-126, miR-210-3p), which enhance endothelial functions and osteogenic differentiation in vitro and in vivo</cite>. <cite id="32374b36-4">Combining exosomes with β-TCP scaffolds in vivo dramatically promotes angiogenesis and bone regeneration</cite>. Biocompatible carriers that preserve exosomal targeting and cargo stability can enhance bone regeneration.

Outlook

Endothelial exosomes provide a natural, paracrine framework for coupling angiogenesis with osteogenesis by integrating metabolic cues (hypoxia/HIF-1α), endothelial–osteogenic feedback loops (BTBD16, lncRNA-H19/Angpt1–Tie2), and cargo-controlled modulation of osteoclasts via miR-155 and MALAT1. <cite id="763527d1-2">EC-Exos initiate positive feedback between osteogenesis and angiogenesis by shaping osteogenic and endothelial phenotypes</cite>, while <cite id="763527d1-4">EC-derived exosomes promote bone regeneration and prevent osteoporosis and osteonecrosis through miRNA-mediated mechanisms</cite>. <cite id="32374b36-1">Hypoxia-polarized exosomes that co-deliver miR-210-3p and miR-1260a or miR-126 synergistically enhance angiogenesis and osteogenesis in vivo</cite>, and <cite id="dca1ceb9-1">miR-155-loaded EC exosomes can tilt the balance toward bone formation by suppressing SOCS1/RANKL-driven osteoclastogenesis</cite>. As materials and cargo engineering mature, endothelial exosomes may be optimized as bone-targeted therapeutics that orchestrate vascularization, osteogenic differentiation, and remodeling homeostasis while mitigating pro-resorptive inflammation. <cite id="763527d1-0">Emerging pathways such as PERK–ATF4–CRELD2 suggest additional metabolic coupling mechanisms yet to be fully mapped</cite>, providing opportunities to refine exosome-based strategies for precise coupling of angiogenesis with osteogenesis in bone repair and disease.

Key Definitions and Abbreviations

- EC-Exos/EPC-Exos: endothelial cell/endothelial progenitor cell-derived exosomes.
- H-ECs: type H endothelial cells with periendothelial osteogenic potential.
- BTBD16/BTBD: BTB domain-containing 16; BTB/POZ zinc-finger protein family involved in transcriptional regulation.
- lncRNA-H19: long non-coding RNA H19 encoding Angpt1 to activate Tie2 signaling.
- miR-1260a, miR-210-3p, miR-126, miR-155, miR-21, miR-31a-5p, miR-145, miR-27a, miR-124: microRNAs mediating endothelial, osteogenic, and osteoclastogenic programs.
- CRELD2: carboxypeptidase-like domain-containing protein 2; unfolded protein response-related protein implicated in endothelial-to-osteogenic coupling per reported pathway.
</answer>

Title: Exosomes in Bone Generation and Repair: Focusing on Bone Microenvironmental Crosstalk and Engineering Biomaterial Designs
Snippet: Bone formation is an intricate process that requires exquisite coordination among various cellular functions. Previous studies have focused primarily on stimulating the individual functions of cells. However, bone is recognized as a complex structure that is highly vascularized. 86 The blood vessels within bone deliver vital elements, including oxygen, nutrients, and growth factors, and cells, such as immune, stem, or precursor cells, to the surrounding microenvironment. This finding raises an important question: how does cell-to-cell communication and crosstalk between different functions occur? As research progresses, osteogenesis and angiogenesis have been shown to exhibit close spatiotemporal coordination during bone formation. 87 Exosomes have been identified as key players in paracrine signaling, serving as crucial carriers for intercellular communication. Notably, in a rat model of stabilized fracture, a previous study demonstrated that exosomes derived from human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells accelerate fracture healing via HIF-1α-driven angiogenesis. 88 Furthermore, the role of exosomes in osteogenesis-angiogenesis coupling has been revealed to be more complex. Studies have shown that exosomes derived from endothelial cells (EC-Exos) initiate a positive feedback mechanism in the interplay between osteogenesis and angiogenesis. 87 From a mechanistic perspective, EC-Exos increase the expression of BTB domain-containing 16 in BMSCs, facilitating the transformation of the osteoprogenitor phenotype. Osteoprogenitors facilitate the development of type H endothelial cells (H-ECs) by triggering HIF-1α signaling, thereby enhancing the osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs. Furthermore, the use of BMSC-Exos during the osteogenesis-angiogenesis coupling process is of significant interest. Molecular biology experiments have provided detailed insights indicating that BMSC-derived exosomes effectively stimulate the osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs and angiogenesis in ECs. These effects are associated with an increased presence of lncRNA-19 in BMSC-derived exosomes, which facilitates the interaction between BMSCs and ECs during bone homeostasis through the lnc-H19-Angpt1/Tie2 signaling pathway. 89

Title: Bone Cell Exosomes and Emerging Strategies in Bone Engineering
Snippet: Angiogenesis/neovascularization has a key role in bone microenvironment ensuring remodeling and repair. Osteogenesis is known to be closely coupled with angiogenesis during neo-bone formation. Endothelial cell-derived exosomes are able to efficiently target bone cells to stimulate bone regeneration (Table 2). In a study of distraction osteogenesis, endothelial progenitor cells (EPC)-derived exosomes were able to accelerate bone formation by stimulating angiogenesis via Raf/ERK signaling involving upregulation of miR-126 [124]. These results were supported by the induction of in vitro osteoblast differentiation of bone marrow stromal cells mediated by EPC-derived extracellular vesicles [125]. In another study, EPC were shown to promote healing and neovascularization in a mice bone fracture model through recruitment of osteoclast precursors. EPC-derived exosomes enhanced osteoclastic differentiation of bone marrow macrophages through long non-coding RNA-Metastasis-Associated lung adenocarcinoma Transcript-1(MALAT1), which negatively regulated miR-124 [126]. EPC also prevent osteoporosis through promotion of osteogenesis or inhibition of osteoclastogenesis. EC-derived exosomes were found to be internalized more efficiently by bone marrow macrophages than osteoblasts or mesenchymal stem cells. Further, these exosomes are able to inhibit osteoclasts through upregulation of miR-155 and, thus, shown to play role in preventing osteoporosis in mice models [127]. In a bioinformatics study, it was noticed that EPC-derived EVs were able to inhibit mouse glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis through a ferroptotic pathway in osteoblasts [128]. Endothelial cell-derived exosome can prevent osteonecrosis through promotion of osteogenesis via miR-27-a [129]. This confirms the role of endothelial cell-derived exosomes in bone repair and as a possible therapy for bone resorption disorders.

snippet.text: Bone formation is an intricate process that requires exquisite coordination among various cellular functions. Previous studies have focused primarily on stimulating the individual functions of cells. However, bone is recognized as a complex structure that is highly vascularized. 86 The blood vessels within bone deliver vital elements, including oxygen, nutrients, and growth factors, and cells, such as immune, stem, or precursor cells, to the surrounding microenvironment. This finding raises an important question: how does cell-to-cell communication and crosstalk between different functions occur? As research progresses, osteogenesis and angiogenesis have been shown to exhibit close spatiotemporal coordination during bone formation. 87 Exosomes have been identified as key players in paracrine signaling, serving as crucial carriers for intercellular communication. Notably, in a rat model of stabilized fracture, a previous study demonstrated that exosomes derived from human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells accelerate fracture healing via HIF-1α-driven angiogenesis. 88 Furthermore, the role of exosomes in osteogenesis-angiogenesis coupling has been revealed to be more complex. Studies have shown that exosomes derived from endothelial cells (EC-Exos) initiate a positive feedback mechanism in the interplay between osteogenesis and angiogenesis. 87 From a mechanistic perspective, EC-Exos increase the expression of BTB domain-containing 16 in BMSCs, facilitating the transformation of the osteoprogenitor phenotype. Osteoprogenitors facilitate the development of type H endothelial cells (H-ECs) by triggering HIF-1α signaling, thereby enhancing the osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs. Furthermore, the use of BMSC-Exos during the osteogenesis-angiogenesis coupling process is of significant interest. Molecular biology experiments have provided detailed insights indicating that BMSC-derived exosomes effectively stimulate the osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs and angiogenesis in ECs. These effects are associated with an increased presence of lncRNA-19 in BMSC-derived exosomes, which facilitates the interaction between BMSCs and ECs during bone homeostasis through the lnc-H19-Angpt1/Tie2 signaling pathway. 89

snippet.text: Angiogenesis/neovascularization has a key role in bone microenvironment ensuring remodeling and repair. Osteogenesis is known to be closely coupled with angiogenesis during neo-bone formation. Endothelial cell-derived exosomes are able to efficiently target bone cells to stimulate bone regeneration (Table 2). In a study of distraction osteogenesis, endothelial progenitor cells (EPC)-derived exosomes were able to accelerate bone formation by stimulating angiogenesis via Raf/ERK signaling involving upregulation of miR-126 [124]. These results were supported by the induction of in vitro osteoblast differentiation of bone marrow stromal cells mediated by EPC-derived extracellular vesicles [125]. In another study, EPC were shown to promote healing and neovascularization in a mice bone fracture model through recruitment of osteoclast precursors. EPC-derived exosomes enhanced osteoclastic differentiation of bone marrow macrophages through long non-coding RNA-Metastasis-Associated lung adenocarcinoma Transcript-1(MALAT1), which negatively regulated miR-124 [126]. EPC also prevent osteoporosis through promotion of osteogenesis or inhibition of osteoclastogenesis. EC-derived exosomes were found to be internalized more efficiently by bone marrow macrophages than osteoblasts or mesenchymal stem cells. Further, these exosomes are able to inhibit osteoclasts through upregulation of miR-155 and, thus, shown to play role in preventing osteoporosis in mice models [127]. In a bioinformatics study, it was noticed that EPC-derived EVs were able to inhibit mouse glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis through a ferroptotic pathway in osteoblasts [128]. Endothelial cell-derived exosome can prevent osteonecrosis through promotion of osteogenesis via miR-27-a [129]. This confirms the role of endothelial cell-derived exosomes in bone repair and as a possible therapy for bone resorption disorders.

Title: Mesenchymal Stem Cell-Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Bone-Related Diseases: Intercellular Communication Messengers and Therapeutic Engineering Protagonists
Snippet: Previous evidence has revealed that angiogenesis in bone is coupled with osteogenesis, indicating the existence of molecular crosstalk between endothelial and osteoblastic cells. 68,69 Exosomes may function as one of the underlying molecular regulators. Several studies suggested that exosomes from MSCs exert a critical effect on the neo-osteogenesis through simultaneous osteogenesis and angiogenesis. 70,71 These MSC-exosomes could be internalized by the host endogenous progenitors such as osteoblast precursor cells or vascular endothelial cells followed by the up-regulation of osteogenesis-or angiogenesis-related genes, which is mainly caused by the exosomal signaling. For example, the exosomes derived from BMSCs exhibited the ability to expedite both the proliferation and migration of human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) and mouse embryo osteoblast precursor cells and contributed to bone fracture healing eventually. 71 The transplantation of exosomes extracted from the human umbilical cord under hypoxia (hypo-exos) effectively enhanced the healing process of bone fracture. Subsequent investigation revealed that this phenomenon occurs as a result of hypo-exos facilitating the transfer of exosomal miR-126, thereby promoting proliferation, migration, and tube formation in recipient HUVECs. 72 Similarly, exosomes secreted by endothelial progenitor cells could enhance the angiogenic potential of endothelial cells in a manner depended on exosomal miR-126 and ensure the acceleration of distraction osteogenesis. 73 Furthermore, the miR-126 has been found to be associated with the SPRED1/Ras/Erk signaling pathway. 72,73 In addition, the functional role of long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) through exosome cargo in regulating angiogenesis and osteogenesis has also been elucidated in the CBS +/-mice model, a mouse model of skeletal loss associated with mutation in the Cystathionine β-synthase (CBS) enzyme.

Title: Stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles -mediated bone regeneration: mechanisms, targeted delivery, and clinical perspectives in promoting angiogenesis
Snippet: In a mouse calvarial defect model, a single implantation improved BMD and BV/TV and increased CD31 + /α-SMA + microvessels. Mechanistically, miR-1260a coordinately activated osteogenic and angiogenic programs by targeting HDAC7 in osteoblast-lineage cells and COL4A2 in endothelial cells (Wu et al., 2021). 

Hypoxic preconditioning has likewise been shown to remodel exosomal miRNA profiles and amplify vascularized osteogenesis. Exosomes derived from SHED cultured at 2% O 2 ("Hypo-exos") more strongly promoted HUVEC proliferation, migration, and tube formation than normoxic controls and increased CD31 + luminal structures and VEGF signaling. Mechanistic analyses suggested that hypoxia-enriched let-7f-5p increases VEGF by suppressing AGO1, whereas miR-210-3p relieves angiogenic inhibition by targeting EphrinA3, with cooperative enhancement of vascular formation. Hypoxia also increased HIF-1α and the exosome secretion regulator Rab27a in donor cells, implying that hypoxia affects both miRNA loading and vesicle release (Liu et al., 2022). Consistently, exosomes secreted by MSCs preconditioned at 1% O 2 enhanced endothelial angiogenic functions in vitro and increased BV/TV and neovessel volume in calvarial defect models, while also promoting formation of bone-associated H-type vessels (CD31 + /Emcn + ). Mechanistically, hypoxia increased exosomal miR-210-3p, which entered recipient cells and activated the PI3K/AKT axis by directly suppressing EFNA3; miR-210-3p knockdown diminished the pro-angiogenic/ pro-osteogenic effects, whereas EFNA3 inhibition partially rescued these phenotypes (Zhuang et al., 2022).

Snippet: Angiogenic miRNA, found in Li10 exosome included miRNA-125, miR-210-3p, miRNA-126, miR-942-5p, and miRNA-26. Finally, the antiinflammatory activities of miRNA-125, miR-320d, miR-193b-3p, miR-210-3p, and miR-18a-5p were evaluated. In the miRNA DEG results, miR-210-3p was predicted to be highly correlated with the three miR-NAs functionally expressed in cells, followed by miR-125, which has a high potential to regulate angiogenesis and anti-inflammation. In previous studies, miR-210-3p was found to work through the EFNA3/PI3K/ AKT pathway by utilizing hypo-sEVs and can be useful for enhancing vascularized bone regeneration [51]. Other studies have indicated that miR-210-3p enhances osteogenic gene expression in vitro and promotes subcutaneous critical-size load-bearing bone defects in a mouse model of bone regeneration using miR-210-3p/β-tricalcium phosphate (β-TCP) with bone marrow stem cells [52]. In recent studies on miR-210-3p, hUCMSC-derived exosomes were found to improve cardiac function by targeting EFNA3 to improve the angiogenesis of miR-210-3p, promote angiogenesis around the heart, promote proliferation, inhibit cell apoptosis, and reduce fibrosis [50]. These results demonstrate that Li10-stimulated exosomes have high application value for tissue regeneration. Furthermore, the GO terms enriched in Li10 up-regulated genes were significantly correlated with actin cytosol, cytoplasm, protein phosphorylation, cell membrane, endoplasmic reticulum membrane, and bone regeneration processes (Fig. 7H). To further investigate the possible mechanisms underlying the effects of miRNAs on osteoblast function, the upregulated miRNAs were subjected to GO and KEGG analyses to identify the pathways controlled by Li10.

Title: Mesenchymal Stem Cell-Derived Exosomes Enhance 3D-Printed Scaffold Functions and Promote Alveolar Bone Defect Repair by Enhancing Angiogenesis
Snippet: Angiogenesis plays an important role in the progression of osteogenesis, as the blood supply provides sufficient oxygen and nutrients and induces the migration of osteoblasts and the mineralization of bone tissue [30,31]. Recent studies have reported that exosomes have various potential applications in diagnosis and treatment. Exosomes have been suggested as potential regenerative agents that can replace stem cell transplantation in bone regeneration, as they deliver bioactive molecules to enhance angiogenesis and osteogenesis [32,33]. Exosomes from stem cells have the potential to be combined with bone-engineering scaffolds to repair bone defects [34]. Exosome-mediated angiogenesis has been reported. MSC-Exos can promote the proliferation, migration, and angiogenic differentiation of endothelial progenitor cells (EPCs) [35]. Mechanistic studies revealed that exosomal miR-21 promotes angiogenesis by upregulating the NOTCH1/DLL4 pathway [35]. Other reports have shown that MSC-derived exosomal miR-21 targets SPRY2 to enhance angiogenesis and exosomal miR-1260a via the inhibition of COL4A2 to promote angiogenesis [36,37]. Jing et al. reported that stem cells from apical-papilla-derived exosomes promote angiogenesis via miR-126-5p, as indicated by increased expression of VEGF and ANG-1 [38]. Additionally, Takeuchi et al. revealed that MSC-Exos promoted the expression of not only osteogenesis-related genes, but also angiogenesis-related genes such as VEGF, ANG1, and ANG2 [31]. In vivo experiments revealed that the application of exosomes secreted by human-induced pluripotent-stem-cell-derived mesenchymal stem cell (hiPSC-MSC-Exo)+β-TCP scaffolds dramatically promoted angiogenesis and bone regeneration in critical-sized calvarial defects in ovariectomized rats [39].

Title: How exosomal platelet-derived miRNAs can lead to spontaneous osteoclastogenesis in osteoporosis: a new mechanistic viewpoint
Snippet: This context-dependent regulation highlights the dynamic nature of exosomal miRNA-mediated communication in bone remodeling. 

(v) Platelet-Derived miRs shaping endothelial contributions to osteoclastogenesis Bone marrow endothelial cells, particularly those lining the sinusoids, represent highly sensitive targets of P-EXOs, even under physiological conditions. In this context, several P-EXO-derived miRs may contribute in a complementary manner. miR-155, through direct repression of SOCS1, promotes macrophage polarization toward an M1 phenotype, prolongs activation of the JAK/STAT1 pathway, and enhances the secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines such as TNF-α and IL-6 (57, 78). Similarly, miR-21 suppresses SOCS1 and SOCS3, thereby amplifying inflammatory responses in both endothelial cells and macrophages, whereas miR-126 regulates vascular permeability and increases the chemoattractive capacity of endothelial cells, facilitating the recruitment of circulating monocytes into the bone marrow (79,80). Endothelial activation mediated by these miRs leads to overproduction of cytokines and growth factors such as IL-6, IL-8, MCP-1 (CCL2), GM-CSF, and G-CSF (81). Title: Microbial messengers: decoding the gut microbiota’s role in bone health through immunomodulation and exosomal signaling
Snippet: Endothelial cell (EC)-derived exosomes contribute to vascular support for bone health. Abnormal angiogenesis with increased osteoclast function is a defining feature of bone resorption and is linked to osteoporosis 172 . EC-derived exosomes rich in miR-126, miR-31, and miR-155 affect bone remodeling by promoting angiogenesis and osteogenesis and inhibiting osteoclast generation. Specifically, miR-126 promotes bone formation via the PI3K/Akt/eNOS pathway, increasing blood flow and nutrient supply to osteoblasts, while miR-155 inhibits osteoclast development by reducing SOCS-1 and RANKL signaling 173 . GM imbalance can trigger systemic inflammation and osteoclast production due to intestinal barrier failure and endotoxin translocation 174 . Notably, GM modulates the cargo and release of EC-derived exosomes, which in turn regulate intestinal health and immune responses 25 . Osteocyte-derived exosomes serve as guardians of bone integrity. Osteocytes, the most abundant and long-lived bone cells, secrete exosomes rich in microRNAs, long non-coding RNAs, proteins, and signaling lipids, which regulate osteoblast and osteoclast activity 175 . Exosomes from mechanically stimulated osteocytes can restore osteogenic activity in aged or osteoporotic bone 176  osteoblast activity via Wnt/β-catenin and BMP pathways 177 . Osteocyte exosomes can also carry anti-inflammatory miRNAs that regulate intestinal epithelial cells or immune cells in gut-associated lymphoid tissue, thereby improving intestinal barrier function and reducing chronic low-grade inflammation 178 . Conversely, in diabetes, osteocytes secrete exosomes with elevated miR-124-3p, which contributes to bone degradation by impairing osteoblasts 105 . Furthermore, exosomes produced from osteocytes and nonosteocytes have been found to play a significant role in the regulation of bone homeostasis.

Title: Exosomes: A Friend or Foe for Osteoporotic Fracture?
Snippet: Blood vessels occupy vital positions in bone homeostasis. Endothelial cells are stationed at the inner layer of vascular vessels, which actively participate in the progress of internalizing and secreting substances like exosomes. Song et al. found that miR-155 loaded in endothelial cells-derived exosomes suppressed osteoclasts' differentiation and activation by several targets, like Spi1, microphthalmia-associated transcription factor (Mitf), and suppressor of cytokine signaling 1 (Socs1) (67). Furthermore, endothelial cells-derived exosomes could rescue the glucocorticoid-induced osteogenic suppression of osteoblasts by inhibiting ferritinophagy-dependent ferroptosis (68). Hence, endothelial cells-derived exosomes might be promising and biocompatible nanomedicine for OP.

Title: Effects of exosomes from different origins on osteoclasts
Snippet: Vascular cells play an integral role in bone repair and homeostasis, not only through angiogenesis but also via paracrine signaling mediated by exosomes. CuiY et al. found that exosomes derived from endothelial progenitor cells had a higher level of MALAT1 expression than those in endothelial progenitor cells, suggesting that MALAT1 in endothelial progenitor cells may play a role by migrating into exosomes. Exosomes derived from endothelial progenitor cells were found to promote the recruitment and differentiation of osteoclast progenitors by delivering MALAT1 targeting miR-214 [56]. Pericytes, derived from the inner wall of blood vessels, influence organ development and tissue homeostasis by producing paracrine signaling molecules [57]. In the skeletal system, vascular factors secreted by pericytes and angiogenic factors secreted by bone cells co-regulate angiogenesis and bone formation. CaiM et al. demonstrated that conditional deletion of pericytes in vivo would promote bone resorption leading to bone loss. Mechanically, pericellular-derived exosomes inhibit osteoclast differentiation and bone resorption by transducing tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated factor 3 (Traf3) to inhibit NF-κB signaling [58]. Targeted therapy is one of the important ways to reduce adverse drug reactions. SongH et al. provided evidence in a mouse model that vascular endothelial cell-derived exosomes have good bone targeting and biological adaptability, and found that vascular endothelial cell-derived exosomes inhibit osteoclast differentiation and function by delivering miR-155 [59].

Title: Advances in the application of mesenchymal stem cells, exosomes, biomimetic materials, and 3D printing in osteoporosis treatment
Snippet: Xu et al. reported that high levels of microRNA-31a-5p (miR-31a-5p) in BMMSCs increased osteoclast formation, resulting in age-related bone loss, whereas introduction of antagomiR-31a-5p in the bone marrow microenvironment inhibited mir-31a-5p, thereby reducing osteoclast activity [50]. Additionally, Song et al. found that exosomes secreted by vascular endothelial cells (EC-Exos) had better bone-targeting activity. After absorbing EC-Exos, bone marrow-derived macrophages strongly express miR-155 and inhibit the induction of osteoclasts, thereby treating osteoporosis [51].

A retrieval system can survey papers on exosome-mediated angiogenesis, osteogenesis separately, and papers describing their co-occurrence. However, 'coupling' implies a causal directional relationship—does angiogenesis drive osteogenesis via exosomes, or vice versa, or is it bidirectional feedback? The mechanism's directionality and temporal sequence matter for understanding the biology but may not be consistently established across studies that simply show correlation or co-occurrence. I could require disambiguating correlation from causation, but that's somewhat generic.
