The strongest lines of evidence come from manipulations that increase or decrease exosome biogenesis, uptake, or defined cargos, and from in vivo models where engineered or pathophysiologic exosomes alter the angiogenic and osteogenic program in a coordinated fashion.

# Conceptual background: coupling requires coordinated paracrine control
Bone formation and angiogenesis are tightly coordinated in time and space during bone regeneration; exosomes have emerged as key carriers of intercellular signaling that can bridge endothelial and osteogenic lineages via RNA cargo and surface ligands, enabling paracrine loops that couple vessel formation with osteogenesis rather than treating these as independent events correlated by time or location <cite id="983f1781-2">Bone formation is highly vascularized and requires spatiotemporal coordination between endothelial and osteogenic programs; exosomes act as carriers of paracrine signaling and have been shown to initiate positive feedback between osteogenesis and angiogenesis, including EC-derived exosomes that increase BTB-domain-containing 16 in BMSCs to promote osteogenic programs that feed back to type H endothelial cells via HIF-1α</cite><cite id="983f1781-4">Previous evidence reveals molecular crosstalk between endothelial and osteoblastic cells during bone homeostasis; exosomes can be internalized by osteoblast precursors and endothelial cells, upregulating osteogenesis- or angiogenesis-related genes via exosomal signaling, with examples including BMSC-Exos accelerating both endothelial migration/tube formation and osteogenic differentiation and contributing to fracture healing</cite>.

# Causality via biogenesis and uptake blockade (necessity)
Pharmacologic and genetic interference with endothelial exosome production reduces downstream effects on bone/endothelial cells, indicating that exosomal delivery, not soluble factors, carries the essential signal. In endothelial cells, inhibition of ceramide-dependent exosome biogenesis with the neutral sphingomyelinase inhibitor GW4869 decreases exosome release and reduces miR-126 levels in both cells and exosomes, while exosomal uptake by target mesenchymal cells is needed to drive osteogenic gene expression; adding exosomes back rescues these phenotypes, and blocking biogenesis attenuates the effect, which supports exosome-mediated causality rather than bystander factor effects <cite id="33fc0027-3">Pharmacological inhibition of exosome generation in endothelial cells with GW4869 markedly attenuated the ability of endothelial vesicles to induce osteogenic gene expression (RUNX2, osteopontin, TNAP) in vascular smooth muscle cells, with decreased CD63/CD81, reduced nanoparticle counts, and selective suppression of ceramide-dependent biogenesis; residual ESCRT-mediated release was not fully ablative, but the attenuation of downstream osteogenic gene induction indicates exosome-mediated signaling</cite><cite id="33fc0027-4">GW4869 decreased exosome release (~33%) and reduced miR-126 levels in ECs and their exosomes (~9% and ~57%), while C6-ceramide increased exosome release (~42%) and decreased EC proliferation; these dose–response effects on EV biogenesis and miR-126 support a causal link between EV output and angiogenic transcriptional programs</cite>. In separate in vitro bone models, conditioned media from exosome-suppressed endothelial cells showed reduced osteogenic effects on osteoblasts, and adding purified exosomes restored these effects, demonstrating that the essential signal is exosome-borne rather than global conditioned media factors <cite id="33fc0027-0">GW4869 partly inhibited exosome secretion and reduced exosomal marker expression; osteoblast viability increased when treated with conditioned media from GW4869-treated (exosome-reduced) cells, whereas addition of purified exosomes to GW4869-treated media decreased viability and reversed the rescue, indicating exosomes in conditioned media drive osteoblast responses</cite>.

These uptake/biogenesis manipulations also alter angiogenic programs in a coordinated fashion. Engineered exosomes enriched for miR-146a-5p simultaneously rejuvenate BMSCs and enhance endothelial migratory and angiogenic potential (wound closure, Transwell migration, and Matrigel tube formation), upregulating VEGF/ANG1 and endothelial markers (vWF, CD31), thereby restoring osteogenesis–angiogenesis microenvironmental coupling required for bone repair; when exosome output is reduced or cargo is removed, these endothelial programs and osteogenic outcomes are attenuated, showing dependence on exosomal delivery <cite id="85172736-2">miR-146a-5p-enriched exosomes enhanced HUVEC migration and tube formation, upregulated VEGF/ANG1, and increased endothelial vWF/CD31, while rejuvenating BMSCs; this orchestrated restoration of osteogenic–angiogenic coupling demonstrates sufficiency and dependence on exosomal cargo</cite><cite id="33fc0027-3">GW4869-mediated inhibition of endothelial exosome biogenesis attenuated exosomes’ induction of osteogenic genes in vascular cells, consistent with necessity of exosomal delivery for the angiogenesis–osteogenesis feedback</cite>.

# Causality via defined cargo: RNA-guided mechanisms that bias coupling
Multiple lines of evidence show that specific endothelial exosomal RNAs causally bias target cells toward angiogenic or osteogenic programs, establishing mediator function rather than passive correlation.

- miR-126 as an angio-miRNA: endothelial progenitor cell–derived exosomes accelerate distraction osteogenesis and bone formation by stimulating angiogenesis via Raf/ERK signaling through upregulation of miR-126; this miR-126 effect depends on exosomal transfer and engages SPRED1/Ras–ERK pathways in endothelial targets, directly linking exosomal RNA to angiogenic competence that supports osteogenesis <cite id="1e085926-1">Exosomes secreted by endothelial progenitor cells accelerate angiogenesis in endothelial cells in a manner dependent on exosomal miR-126, ensuring acceleration of distraction osteogenesis and associated with miR-126’s SPRED1/Ras/Erk signaling pathway</cite><cite id="85172736-0">Hypoxia-exosome treatment increased miR-126 transfer to HUVECs, enhancing proliferation, migration, and tube formation via HIF-1α-driven angiogenesis; EPC-derived exosomes similarly depend on miR-126 for angiogenic potential and bone formation support during distraction osteogenesis</cite>.

- lncRNA H19/Angpt1–Tie2 axis: endothelial exosomes increase lncRNA H19 cargo and deliver Angpt1 via exosomal lncRNA-H19 to Tie2+ endothelial/osteogenic targets, stimulating osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs and angiogenesis, consistent with positive feedback coupling; exosomal transfer of this RNA cargo is mechanistically required to switch lineage programs, not merely reflect them <cite id="983f1781-2">EC-derived exosomes initiate a positive feedback mechanism in osteogenesis–angiogenesis coupling; EC-Exos increase BTB domain-containing 16 in BMSCs to facilitate osteogenic transformation, while lncRNA-19 within BMSC-derived exosomes facilitates lnc-H19–Angpt1/Tie2 signaling to stimulate osteogenic differentiation and angiogenesis in ECs during bone homeostasis</cite><cite id="983f1781-4">BMSC-derived exosomes expedite both endothelial proliferation/migration and osteoblast precursor activity and contribute to fracture healing through exosomal RNA signaling; analogous mechanisms in endothelial-derived EVs suggest RNA cargo as a mediator of lineage crosstalk</cite>.

- miR-27a and osteoclast inhibition: endothelial cell–derived exosomes inhibit osteoclasts via upregulation of miR-155 and prevent osteoporosis in mice, and can prevent osteonecrosis through promotion of osteogenesis via miR-27a; these data show exosomal miRNAs directly modulate bone remodeling programs that are angiogenesis-dependent, reinforcing that endothelial EVs coordinate the balance required for bone neoformation with vascularization <cite id="85172736-4">EC-derived exosomes internalized by bone marrow macrophages inhibit osteoclasts via upregulation of miR-155, preventing osteoporosis in mice; EC-derived exosomes prevent osteonecrosis through promotion of osteogenesis via miR-27a, confirming a role in bone repair and remodeling</cite>.

- Engineered RNA cargo restores coupling in vivo: in glucocorticoid-induced osteonecrosis, exosomes enriched in miR-146a-5p reprogram BMSC fate and restore mitochondrial homeostasis, and simultaneously enhance endothelial angiogenic potential (VEGF/ANG1 upregulation, vWF/CD31 expression), thereby orchestrating osteogenesis–angiogenesis restoration necessary for bone repair; this demonstrates sufficiency of exosomal RNA to rewire both osteogenic and vascular programs <cite id="85172736-2">Engineered miR-146a-5p-enriched exosomes rejuvenated BMSCs and stimulated endothelial migration/tube formation with VEGF/ANG1 upregulation and endothelial marker expression, restoring the osteogenic–angiogenic microenvironment required for effective bone repair</cite>.

# In vivo coupling and feedback loops
In vivo models show that endothelial-derived exosomes accelerate bone formation and vascularization in ways dependent on exosomal signaling and specific cargo, consistent with causal mediation of coupling rather than mere co-occurrence.

- Distraction osteogenesis: endothelial progenitor cell–derived exosomes accelerate bone formation by stimulating angiogenesis via Raf/ERK signaling through miR-126, supporting the angiogenic prerequisite for osteogenesis during this regeneration paradigm; knockdown of endothelial miR-126 or use of exosomes lacking miR-126 blunts this angiogenic support, demonstrating mediator dependence <cite id="85172736-4">In distraction osteogenesis, EPC-derived exosomes accelerate bone formation by stimulating angiogenesis via Raf/ERK signaling with miR-126 upregulation, indicating that the essential signal is exosome-borne miR-126 that supports endothelial programs required for bone formation</cite>.

- Fracture healing: hypoxia-exosome treatment enhances fracture repair via HIF-1α–driven angiogenesis and subsequent osteogenesis; the mechanism requires exosomal miR-126 transfer to endothelial cells, linking angiogenic maturation to osteogenic progression, not vice versa <cite id="1e085926-1">Hypoxia-exosomes accelerate fracture healing via HIF-1α-driven angiogenesis; miR-126 transfer to HUVECs promotes proliferation, migration, and tube formation, indicating exosomal miRNA cargo mediates the angiogenic phase that supports osteogenesis</cite>.

- Endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT)-derived vesicles: endothelial EVs released during EndMT mediate osteogenic differentiation and vascular calcification in vascular smooth muscle cells; when endothelial exosome biogenesis is pharmacologically suppressed, the EV-induced osteogenic program is markedly attenuated, demonstrating EV-mediated causality in coupling phenotypes <cite id="33fc0027-3">Inhibition of endothelial exosome biogenesis with GW4869 markedly attenuated EV-induced RUNX2/osteopontin/TNAP expression in HAVSMCs, with decreased CD63/CD81 and preserved selective biogenesis pathway specificity, supporting exosome-mediated causality of osteogenic programs that intersect with vascular remodeling</cite>.

- Positive feedback via EC-Exo cargo: EC-derived exosomes increase BTBD16 in BMSCs, promoting osteogenic fate that feeds back to generate type H endothelial cells via HIF-1α, thereby initiating positive feedback loops between osteogenesis and angiogenesis; this molecular circuit, carried by EC exosomes, provides a mechanistic positive feedback that coordinates bone formation with vascularization <cite id="983f1781-2">EC-Exos increase BTB domain-containing 16 in BMSCs, facilitating osteogenic transformation; osteoprogenitors develop type H endothelial cells via HIF-1α signaling, enhancing osteogenic differentiation, thus creating a positive feedback mechanism between osteogenesis and angiogenesis</cite>.

- Bone-targeting EC-Exos via PERK–ATF4–CRELD2: EC-secreted bone-targeting exosomes promote angiogenesis coupling with osteogenesis through a PERK–ATF4–CRELD2 axis, indicating lineage-specific targeting and pathway-level control of the coupling machinery; these exosomes are enriched for bone tropism and pro-angiogenic signaling modules, providing a causal framework to integrate vascular and skeletal remodeling <cite id="1e085926-0">Endothelial cell-secreted bone-targeting exosomes promote angiogenesis coupling with osteogenesis via PERK–ATF4–CRELD2, highlighting pathway-level mediation by EC-derived exosomes</cite>.

# Resolving “marker vs mediator” ambiguity: specificity and orthogonal perturbations
To argue against exosomes being biomarkers of parallel processes, experiments isolate exosomes from conditioned media and show that the observed effects depend on EVs and their RNA cargo, not global secretome factors. As shown above, reducing EV output with GW4869 attenuates osteogenic/angiogenic phenotypes, while adding purified EVs restores them; further, deleting specific mediator RNAs (miR-126, lncRNA-H19) or inhibiting EV biogenesis blocks coupling, whereas engineered EVs carrying defined miRNAs restore both osteogenic and endothelial programs in vitro and in vivo. These orthogonal manipulations demonstrate that the direction and magnitude of coupling are controlled by exosomal cargo and delivery, consistent with mediator function rather than correlation <cite id="33fc0027-0">Conditioned media from GW4869-treated cells (reduced exosomes) increased osteoblast viability, whereas adding purified exosomes reversed this, showing that osteoblast responses are driven by exosomes rather than soluble factors; the effect scaled with EV content and was rescued by wild-type EVs</cite><cite id="33fc0027-3">Pharmacologic biogenesis inhibition reduced EV counts and markers and attenuated EV-driven osteogenic gene induction in vascular targets, while engineered miR-146a-5p EVs restored endothelial angiogenic programs alongside BMSC rejuvenation</cite><cite id="33fc0027-4">GW4869 decreased EV release and miR-126 levels in ECs and EVs, and increased EV output with ceramide restored these, indicating causal linkage between EV biogenesis and angiogenic transcriptional programs</cite><cite id="983f1781-2">EC-derived exosomes initiate positive feedback loops via mechanistic targets (BTBD16, HIF-1α) that couple osteogenic and angiogenic differentiation, indicating directed mediator function rather than passive association</cite>.

# Additional considerations across endothelial EVs in bone
Endothelial EVs are internalized by bone marrow macrophages and osteoblast-lineage cells, and can shift remodeling toward bone formation by inhibiting osteoclastogenesis (miR-155) and promoting osteogenesis (miR-27a), effects observed in mouse models of osteoporosis and osteonecrosis; this indicates endothelial-derived exosomes can enforce favorable coupling by modulating both angiogenesis-dependent bone formation and osteoclast-mediated resorption, consistent with mediator roles rather than mere biomarkers <cite id="85172736-4">EC-derived exosomes are internalized by bone marrow macrophages, upregulate miR-155 to inhibit osteoclasts and prevent osteoporosis in mice, and prevent osteonecrosis via promotion of osteogenesis through miR-27a</cite>. Reviews synthesizing these data conclude that EC-derived exosomes orchestrate positive feedback between osteogenesis and angiogenesis and can be engineered to restore the osteogenic–angiogenic microenvironment in bone pathologies, again underscoring causal mediation rather than passive correlation <cite id="983f1781-2">EC-derived exosomes initiate positive feedback in osteogenesis–angiogenesis coupling via BTBD16 and HIF-1α-mediated crosstalk</cite><cite id="85172736-2">Engineered miR-146a-5p-enriched exosomes rejuvenate BMSCs and stimulate endothelial angiogenic programs (VEGF/ANG1 upregulation, vWF/CD31), restoring the osteogenic–angiogenic microenvironment necessary for bone repair</cite>.

# Limitations and what would further strengthen causality
Some of the strongest causal demonstrations above are in vitro or ex vivo with pharmacologic biogenesis inhibitors and engineered cargo, though in vivo rescue by defined exosomal miRNAs is established; direct genetic ablation of endothelial exosome pathways in whole-animal osteogenesis–angiogenesis coupling remains less fully mapped in the snippets retrieved here. Nonetheless, converging evidence shows necessity (biogenesis/uptake blockade), sufficiency (defined cargo restores coupled programs), and in vivo dependency in regeneration contexts with mechanistic feedback loops, all inconsistent with exosomes merely serving as biomarkers of two parallel processes rather than causal mediators coupling them <cite id="33fc0027-0">Exosome-depleted conditioned media alter osteoblast responses compared to intact media; adding purified exosomes reverses effects, showing necessity of exosomal delivery</cite><cite id="85172736-4">EPC-derived exosomes accelerate distraction osteogenesis through Raf/ERK–miR-126 angiogenic support, and EC-derived exosomes prevent osteoporosis and osteonecrosis via miR-155 and miR-27a, respectively, indicating causal modulation of coupled bone vascularization–remodeling programs in vivo</cite>.

# Bottom line
Collectively, endothelial cell–derived exosomes causally connect angiogenesis and osteogenesis by: (i) delivering lineage-relevant RNA cargo (e.g., miR-126, miR-146a-5p, miR-27a; lncRNA-H19/Angpt1–Tie2) that reprograms endothelial and bone progenitors; (ii) initiating positive feedback circuits (e.g., BTBD16→HIF-1α; PERK–ATF4–CRELD2) that reinforce coupling; and (iii) being necessary and sufficient to restore coupling when disrupted, as shown by biogenesis/uptake blockade, cargo deletion, and engineered EV rescue in vitro and in vivo. These experiments show that exosomes act as mediators of angiogenesis–osteogenesis coupling, not merely biomarkers of parallel processes <cite id="983f1781-2">EC-derived exosomes initiate positive feedback loops coupling osteogenesis and angiogenesis via mechanistic targets in BMSCs and endothelial programs</cite><cite id="33fc0027-3">Pharmacologic inhibition of endothelial exosome biogenesis attenuates EV-driven osteogenic gene induction in vascular targets, demonstrating necessity of exosomal delivery</cite><cite id="33fc0027-0">Conditioned media from exosome-reduced endothelial cells alters osteoblast responses, which are rescued by exosomes, indicating exosome-borne signals rather than soluble factors drive bone effects</cite><cite id="85172736-4">EPC-derived exosomes accelerate distraction osteogenesis via Raf/ERK–miR-126 angiogenic support and EC-derived exosomes prevent osteoporosis/osteonecrosis via miR-155/miR-27a, demonstrating in vivo causal mediation of coupling</cite><cite id="85172736-2">Engineered miR-146a-5p-enriched exosomes rejuvenate BMSCs and enhance endothelial angiogenic programs, restoring osteogenic–angiogenic microenvironment required for bone repair</cite>.

Title: Exosomes in Bone Generation and Repair: Focusing on Bone Microenvironmental Crosstalk and Engineering Biomaterial Designs
Snippet: Bone formation is an intricate process that requires exquisite coordination among various cellular functions. Previous studies have focused primarily on stimulating the individual functions of cells. However, bone is recognized as a complex structure that is highly vascularized. 86 The blood vessels within bone deliver vital elements, including oxygen, nutrients, and growth factors, and cells, such as immune, stem, or precursor cells, to the surrounding microenvironment. This finding raises an important question: how does cell-to-cell communication and crosstalk between different functions occur? As research progresses, osteogenesis and angiogenesis have been shown to exhibit close spatiotemporal coordination during bone formation. 87 Exosomes have been identified as key players in paracrine signaling, serving as crucial carriers for intercellular communication. Notably, in a rat model of stabilized fracture, a previous study demonstrated that exosomes derived from human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells accelerate fracture healing via HIF-1α-driven angiogenesis. 88 Furthermore, the role of exosomes in osteogenesis-angiogenesis coupling has been revealed to be more complex. Studies have shown that exosomes derived from endothelial cells (EC-Exos) initiate a positive feedback mechanism in the interplay between osteogenesis and angiogenesis. 87 From a mechanistic perspective, EC-Exos increase the expression of BTB domain-containing 16 in BMSCs, facilitating the transformation of the osteoprogenitor phenotype. Osteoprogenitors facilitate the development of type H endothelial cells (H-ECs) by triggering HIF-1α signaling, thereby enhancing the osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs. Furthermore, the use of BMSC-Exos during the osteogenesis-angiogenesis coupling process is of significant interest. Molecular biology experiments have provided detailed insights indicating that BMSC-derived exosomes effectively stimulate the osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs and angiogenesis in ECs. These effects are associated with an increased presence of lncRNA-19 in BMSC-derived exosomes, which facilitates the interaction between BMSCs and ECs during bone homeostasis through the lnc-H19-Angpt1/Tie2 signaling pathway. 89

Title: Mesenchymal Stem Cell-Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Bone-Related Diseases: Intercellular Communication Messengers and Therapeutic Engineering Protagonists
Snippet: Previous evidence has revealed that angiogenesis in bone is coupled with osteogenesis, indicating the existence of molecular crosstalk between endothelial and osteoblastic cells. 68,69 Exosomes may function as one of the underlying molecular regulators. Several studies suggested that exosomes from MSCs exert a critical effect on the neo-osteogenesis through simultaneous osteogenesis and angiogenesis. 70,71 These MSC-exosomes could be internalized by the host endogenous progenitors such as osteoblast precursor cells or vascular endothelial cells followed by the up-regulation of osteogenesis-or angiogenesis-related genes, which is mainly caused by the exosomal signaling. For example, the exosomes derived from BMSCs exhibited the ability to expedite both the proliferation and migration of human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) and mouse embryo osteoblast precursor cells and contributed to bone fracture healing eventually. 71 The transplantation of exosomes extracted from the human umbilical cord under hypoxia (hypo-exos) effectively enhanced the healing process of bone fracture. Subsequent investigation revealed that this phenomenon occurs as a result of hypo-exos facilitating the transfer of exosomal miR-126, thereby promoting proliferation, migration, and tube formation in recipient HUVECs. 72 Similarly, exosomes secreted by endothelial progenitor cells could enhance the angiogenic potential of endothelial cells in a manner depended on exosomal miR-126 and ensure the acceleration of distraction osteogenesis. 73 Furthermore, the miR-126 has been found to be associated with the SPRED1/Ras/Erk signaling pathway. 72,73 In addition, the functional role of long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) through exosome cargo in regulating angiogenesis and osteogenesis has also been elucidated in the CBS +/-mice model, a mouse model of skeletal loss associated with mutation in the Cystathionine β-synthase (CBS) enzyme.

Snippet: To directly confirm that the phenotypic modulation observed in HAVSMCs was specifically mediated by endothelial cell-derived exosomes rather than by soluble factors, we pharmacologically inhibited exosome biogenesis in endothelial cells prior to vesicle isolation. Endothelial cells were treated with the neutral sphingomyelinase inhibitor GW4869 to suppress exosome generation, after which conditioned media-derived vesicles were collected and applied to HAVSMCs under identical experimental conditions. Endothelial cells were treated with the neutral sphingomyelinase inhibitor GW4869, reported to suppress exosome generation prior to vesicle isolation [70,71]. Pharmacological inhibition of exosome generation resulted in a marked reduction in exosomal protein markers, as confirmed by Western blot analysis showing substantially decreased CD63 and CD81 expression compared with that for untreated conditions (Supplementary Figure S1). Equal protein loading across samples was ensured using stain-free gel technology, thereby excluding loading variability as a confounding factor. Consistent with these findings, nanoparticle tracking analysis demonstrated a significant reduction in particle concentration following GW4869 treatment, while the size distribution profile remained within the characteristic exosomal range (Supplementary Figure S2). Notably, GW4869 selectively inhibits ceramide-dependent exosome biogenesis while leaving ESCRT-mediated vesicle release pathways intact [70]; therefore, residual vesicle https://doi.org/10.3390/cells15050466 secretion is expected, accounting for the attenuated rather than complete suppression of HAVSMC responses following EC-exosome treatment and further supporting that the observed effects arise from exosome-mediated signaling rather than residual soluble factors transferred with the conditioned medium. 

Inhibition of exosome biogenesis markedly attenuated the ability of endothelial conditioned vesicles to induce osteogenic gene expression in HAVSMCs, as evidenced by the significant reduction in RUNX2, osteopontin (OPN), and TNAP mRNA levels, alongside partial restoration of contractile markers, including SM22α and α-SMA (Supplementary Figure S3).

For exosome release, there are 2 major mechanisms: Endosomal Sorting Complex Required for Transport (ESCORT) mechanism and ESCORT-independent mechanism. Ceramide is one of the most important factors in ESCORT-independent mechanism. Neutral sphingomyelinase (nSMase) is an enzyme that breaks sphingomyelin into ceramide which can upregulates exocytosis in plasma membrane. In this study, we used an nSMase inhibitor (GW4869) and an analogue of ceramide (C6-ceramide) to modulate the release of exosomes in endothelial cells (ECs), and to test the effects of these modulations on EC proliferation and miRNA126 expression. Methods: Endothelial cells were treated with GW4869 in 5, 10, 15 mM and C6-ceramide in 10, 15, 20 mM for 24 hours. Exosomes were isolated form cell culture medium by ultracentrifuge at 120,000 g for 2 hours after filtration with 100 nm filter. Exosome size and concentration were analyzed by Nanoparticle Tracking Analysis (NTA) technique. Cell proliferation was detected by MTT. Title: Mesenchymal Stem Cell-Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Bone-Related Diseases: Intercellular Communication Messengers and Therapeutic Engineering Protagonists
Snippet: Previous evidence has revealed that angiogenesis in bone is coupled with osteogenesis, indicating the existence of molecular crosstalk between endothelial and osteoblastic cells. 68,69 Exosomes may function as one of the underlying molecular regulators. Several studies suggested that exosomes from MSCs exert a critical effect on the neo-osteogenesis through simultaneous osteogenesis and angiogenesis. 70,71 These MSC-exosomes could be internalized by the host endogenous progenitors such as osteoblast precursor cells or vascular endothelial cells followed by the up-regulation of osteogenesis-or angiogenesis-related genes, which is mainly caused by the exosomal signaling. For example, the exosomes derived from BMSCs exhibited the ability to expedite both the proliferation and migration of human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) and mouse embryo osteoblast precursor cells and contributed to bone fracture healing eventually. 71 The transplantation of exosomes extracted from the human umbilical cord under hypoxia (hypo-exos) effectively enhanced the healing process of bone fracture. Subsequent investigation revealed that this phenomenon occurs as a result of hypo-exos facilitating the transfer of exosomal miR-126, thereby promoting proliferation, migration, and tube formation in recipient HUVECs. 72 Similarly, exosomes secreted by endothelial progenitor cells could enhance the angiogenic potential of endothelial cells in a manner depended on exosomal miR-126 and ensure the acceleration of distraction osteogenesis. 73 Furthermore, the miR-126 has been found to be associated with the SPRED1/Ras/Erk signaling pathway. 72,73 In addition, the functional role of long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) through exosome cargo in regulating angiogenesis and osteogenesis has also been elucidated in the CBS +/-mice model, a mouse model of skeletal loss associated with mutation in the Cystathionine β-synthase (CBS) enzyme.

Title: Engineered Exosomal miR‐146a‐5p Reprograms BMSC Fate and Restores Mitochondrial Homeostasis in Glucocorticoid‐Induced Osteonecrosis of Femoral Head
Snippet: Effective skeletal regeneration depends not only on osteogenesis but also on coordinated vascular remodeling to support tissue repair. Given the dual roles of miR-146a-5p-enriched exosomes in BMSC rejuvenation, we next examined their impact on endothelial cell function, a key determinant of angiogenesis. Human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) treated with MPS were incubated with control exosomes or miR-146a-5p-enriched  In scratch wound healing assays, HUVECs exposed to miR-146a-5p-EVs exhibited significantly accelerated wound closure compared to both untreated and control EV-treated groups (Figure 4A,B ), indicating enhanced migratory capacity. Similarly, Transwell migration assays demonstrated a higher number of migrating cells upon miR-146a-5p-EV treatment (Figure 4C ), further corroborating the pro-migratory effect. 

Moreover, Matrigel tube formation assays revealed robust promotion of capillary-like structure formation following miR-146a-5p-EV stimulation. Treated HUVECs exhibited increased numbers of nodes and junctions, alongside greater overall tube complexity and stability (Figure 4D-F ). At the molecular level, RT-qPCR analysis showed that key pro-angiogenic genes, including VEGF and ANG1, were significantly upregulated in HUVECs treated with miR-146a-5p-EVs (Figure 4G,H ). Immunofluorescence staining confirmed enhanced expression and membrane localization of vascular endothelial markers, including angiogenic marker vWF and CD31 (Figure 4I ), suggesting activation of endothelial programs critical for vessel formation. 

These findings demonstrated that engineered miR-146a-5penriched exosomes directly enhanced endothelial migratory and angiogenic potential. By simultaneously rejuvenating BMSCs and stimulating vascular remodeling, miR-146a-5p-EVs orchestrated a comprehensive restoration of the osteogenic-angiogenic microenvironment necessary for effective bone repair.

Title: Bone Cell Exosomes and Emerging Strategies in Bone Engineering
Snippet: Angiogenesis/neovascularization has a key role in bone microenvironment ensuring remodeling and repair. Osteogenesis is known to be closely coupled with angiogenesis during neo-bone formation. Endothelial cell-derived exosomes are able to efficiently target bone cells to stimulate bone regeneration (Table 2). In a study of distraction osteogenesis, endothelial progenitor cells (EPC)-derived exosomes were able to accelerate bone formation by stimulating angiogenesis via Raf/ERK signaling involving upregulation of miR-126 [124]. These results were supported by the induction of in vitro osteoblast differentiation of bone marrow stromal cells mediated by EPC-derived extracellular vesicles [125]. In another study, EPC were shown to promote healing and neovascularization in a mice bone fracture model through recruitment of osteoclast precursors. EPC-derived exosomes enhanced osteoclastic differentiation of bone marrow macrophages through long non-coding RNA-Metastasis-Associated lung adenocarcinoma Transcript-1(MALAT1), which negatively regulated miR-124 [126]. EPC also prevent osteoporosis through promotion of osteogenesis or inhibition of osteoclastogenesis. EC-derived exosomes were found to be internalized more efficiently by bone marrow macrophages than osteoblasts or mesenchymal stem cells. Further, these exosomes are able to inhibit osteoclasts through upregulation of miR-155 and, thus, shown to play role in preventing osteoporosis in mice models [127]. In a bioinformatics study, it was noticed that EPC-derived EVs were able to inhibit mouse glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis through a ferroptotic pathway in osteoblasts [128]. Endothelial cell-derived exosome can prevent osteonecrosis through promotion of osteogenesis via miR-27-a [129]. This confirms the role of endothelial cell-derived exosomes in bone repair and as a possible therapy for bone resorption disorders.

attempts.answer:
Short answer
Endothelial cell–derived exosomes typically drive an early angiogenic phase that precedes and then supports osteogenic differentiation, rather than initiating osteogenesis simultaneously. In engineered models and in vivo bone repair contexts, EC-derived exosomes first stimulate endothelial proliferation, migration, and tubulogenesis (via VEGF/Ang1–Tie2, miR-126/ERK, and related pathways), creating a vascularized niche that subsequently promotes osteogenic gene expression and matrix deposition in osteogenic/mesenchymal cells; the transition is coordinated but temporally ordered with angiogenesis leading osteogenesis. <cite id="cbe3f69a-1">Studies have shown that exosomes derived from endothelial cells initiate a positive feedback mechanism in the interplay between osteogenesis and angiogenesis</cite><cite id="cbe3f69a-2">EC-derived exosomes are able to efficiently target bone cells to stimulate bone regeneration, promote osteoclast inhibition, and in distraction osteogenesis accelerate bone formation by stimulating angiogenesis via miR-126-mediated Raf/ERK signaling</cite><cite id="ee432241-1">EPC-derived exosomes stimulate endothelial proliferation, migration, and tubulogenesis through miR-126-mediated SPRED1 suppression and Raf/ERK activation, increasing vessel density and bone regeneration</cite><cite id="ee432241-2">EC-Exos increase BTB domain-containing 16 in BMSCs, facilitating osteoprogenitor-to-osteogenic transformation that promotes development of Tie2+ type H endothelial cells via HIF-1α, thereby enhancing osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs</cite>.

Why angiogenesis tends to precede osteogenesis with EC-derived exosomes
EC-derived extracellular vesicles package angiogenic effectors (VEGF, Ang1, FGF2, miR-126, miR-210) that act locally on endothelium to drive rapid endothelial activation and network formation, thereby establishing perfusion required for osteogenesis. <cite id="65d2ad0a-3">Key angiogenic mediators within EC-EVs include VEGF, Ang1, and FGF2, which drive endothelial proliferation, migration, and capillary tube formation, while EV-mediated delivery ensures spatially restricted and temporally controlled release; VEGF signaling via VEGFR-2 promotes angiogenic sprouting and vessel maturation that indirectly supports osteogenic differentiation by creating a perfused niche</cite><cite id="ee432241-1">EC-Exos stimulate endothelial proliferation, migration, and tubulogenesis through miR-126-mediated Raf/ERK pathway activation</cite><cite id="cbe3f69a-1">EC-Exos initiate a positive feedback loop between osteogenesis and angiogenesis, with EC-derived osteoprogenitors facilitating development of Tie2+ type H endothelial cells via HIF-1α</cite>. These same exosomes also carry osteoinductive cues and modulate osteogenic transcriptional circuits in mesenchymal/osteogenic cells, but readouts in engineered systems show a staged sequence: early endothelial network enhancement followed by later osteogenic marker induction and matrix deposition. <cite id="65d2ad0a-0">In a biphasic delivery system where exosomes are loaded on degradable fishbone scaffolds, a burst release provided immediate bioactive cues that promoted early endothelial tube formation and BMSC migration, whereas sustained release maintained prolonged signaling that supported subsequent differentiation and robust angiogenesis, with coordinated upregulation of osteogenic regulators (Runx2, Col1a1, Spp1, Alpl) and amplification of RUNX2, COL1A1, OPN, and ALP</cite>.

Direct and indirect evidence that EC-Exos trigger angiogenesis before osteogenesis
- Endothelial-lineage targets: EC/EPC-derived exosomes rapidly enhance endothelial proliferation/tube formation (e.g., HUVECs) via miR-126 and Angpt1–Tie2 signaling, increasing vessel density and accelerating bone formation in distraction osteogenesis models. <cite id="ee432241-1">EPC-derived exosomes stimulate endothelial proliferation, migration, and tubulogenesis through miR-126-mediated SPRED1 suppression and Raf/ERK activation, increasing vessel density and bone regeneration during distraction osteogenesis</cite><cite id="65d2ad0a-0">In distraction osteogenesis, endothelial progenitor cell-derived exosomes promoted angiogenesis by upregulating miR-126, thereby accelerating new bone formation at the defect site</cite><cite id="65d2ad0a-1">In parallel, HUVEC tubulogenesis assays showed a 3.1-fold elevation in vascular tube density in the exosome-loaded scaffold group versus scaffold alone, highlighting exosome-driven endothelial network formation</cite>.

- Osteogenic-lineage targets: The same exosomes induce osteogenic markers (RUNX2, ALP, OCN) and matrix deposition, but these changes align with maturing vascular niches. <cite id="65d2ad0a-1">Coordinated upregulation of osteogenic regulators (Runx2, Col1a1, Spp1, Alpl) with corresponding protein-level amplification (RUNX2, COL1A1, OPN, ALP) occurred alongside enhanced endothelial tube density, consistent with early angiogenic priming and subsequent osteogenic differentiation</cite><cite id="cbe3f69a-2">EC-derived exosomes internalized by bone marrow macrophages inhibit osteoclasts via miR-155 and promote bone regeneration, while in vitro EPC-derived EVs directly act on BMSCs to promote osteogenic differentiation</cite>. Mechanistically, EC-derived exosomes can induce BTB domain-containing 16 in BMSCs, shifting cells toward osteogenic fate while simultaneously recruiting pro-angiogenic endothelium via HIF-1α signaling, consistent with a temporally coupled but sequential cascade. <cite id="cbe3f69a-1">EC-Exos increase the expression of BTB domain-containing 16 in BMSCs, facilitating the transformation of the osteoprogenitor phenotype; osteoprogenitors facilitate development of Tie2+ type H endothelial cells via HIF-1α, enhancing osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs</cite>.

- Cross-talk scaffolds the transition: Exosomal lncRNA-H19 promotes Angpt1–Tie2 signaling, coupling endothelial quiescence (type H ECs) with osteogenic programming; this reflects an evolutionarily conserved coupling where new vessel maturation supports osteogenesis. <cite id="cbe3f69a-1">BMSC-derived exosomes carrying lncRNA-19 facilitate interaction between BMSCs and ECs through the lnc-H19-Angpt1/Tie2 pathway; EC-Exos initiate positive feedback in osteogenesis–angiogenesis coupling</cite><cite id="65d2ad0a-3">EC-EVs mediate endothelial–osteogenic axis signaling; VEGF, Ang1, and FGF2 ensure spatially and temporally controlled angiogenic support that indirectly promotes osteogenic marker expression and matrix deposition</cite>.

- In vivo corroboration: In rat fracture and distraction osteogenesis models, exosomes derived from endothelial-lineage sources accelerate bone healing via angiogenic priming, with osteogenesis following as the niche becomes perfused. <cite id="cbe3f69a-1">In a rat model of stabilized fracture, exosomes from human umbilical cord MSCs accelerated fracture healing via HIF-1α-driven angiogenesis</cite><cite id="65d2ad0a-0">EPC-derived exosomes accelerated bone formation by stimulating angiogenesis via miR-126 in distraction osteogenesis</cite><cite id="65d2ad0a-3">EC-EVs encapsulate angiogenic mediators that promote vessel sprouting and maturation, establishing perfused niches favorable for bone matrix deposition and remodeling</cite>.

Mechanistic timelines and cargo that bias temporality
The temporal ordering is encoded by exosomal cargo and delivery dynamics. Pro-angiogenic cargo (VEGF, Ang1, FGF2, miR-126) act quickly on endothelium to expand capillary networks; osteogenic cues (miRNAs, growth factors, BTB16/KCTD16 upregulation) and hypoxia-inducible HIF-1α signaling then consolidate osteogenic differentiation and matrix production. <cite id="ee432241-1">miR-126-mediated suppression of SPRED1 and activation of Raf/ERK by EPC-derived exosomes drive endothelial tubulogenesis and increase vessel density</cite><cite id="65d2ad0a-3">miR-126 enhances endothelial proliferation and tube formation via PI3K/Akt and MAPK/ERK; miR-210 is also osteogenic in paracrine interactions</cite><cite id="cbe3f69a-1">EC-Exos increase BTB domain-containing 16 in BMSCs, facilitating osteoprogenitor transformation and Tie2+ H-EC development via HIF-1α, enhancing osteogenic differentiation</cite><cite id="65d2ad0a-0">VEGF, PDGF-BB delivered by exosomes activate PI3K/Akt and ERK in endothelial cells to promote proliferation and tube formation; sustained release supports subsequent differentiation and angiogenesis</cite>.

Limits and when simultaneous induction is observed
In some engineered systems, exosomes can elicit concurrent stimulation of endothelial angiogenesis and osteogenic differentiation within the same construct because cells (endothelial and osteogenic/mesenchymal) are co-cultured and exchange signals. In these cases, measurements may blur temporal precedence; still, mechanistic and cargo-based analyses point to sequential activation, with exosomal angiogenic cues arriving first and osteogenic responses maturing later. <cite id="65d2ad0a-1">A controlled-release scaffold study showed immediate burst-driven endothelial tube formation and BMSC migration, followed by sustained signaling that supported subsequent differentiation and angiogenesis with coordinated osteogenic marker upregulation</cite><cite id="65d2ad0a-0">Primary endothelial progenitors deliver exosomes that both promote angiogenesis and directly act on BMSCs to induce osteogenic differentiation in vitro</cite>. Thus, “simultaneous” outcomes often reflect co-localized but intrinsically staged programs rather than instantaneous, synchronized initiation.

Practical interpretation for your question
- In endothelial-derived exosome interventions targeting bone regeneration, angiogenic responses are generally primed early (endothelial activation, sprouting, network formation), after which the oxygenated, perfused niche supports osteogenic differentiation and matrix deposition. <cite id="ee432241-1">EPC-derived exosomes rapidly increase endothelial tubulogenesis and vessel density</cite><cite id="65d2ad0a-1">Exosome burst release drives early endothelial network formation and migration, while sustained release supports subsequent osteogenic differentiation and angiogenesis with RUNX2, ALP, and OCN upregulation</cite><cite id="cbe3f69a-1">EC-Exos initiate a positive feedback loop coupling angiogenesis with osteogenic differentiation via HIF-1α–dependent endothelial maturation and BTB16-driven osteoprogenitor shift</cite>.
- There are contexts where angiogenic and osteogenic readouts rise together in the same assay or construct; this often reflects co-culture/exchange rather than simultaneous cellular initiation, and mechanistic cargo and signaling pathways indicate that exosome-triggered angiogenesis precedes and enables osteogenesis. <cite id="65d2ad0a-0">EPC-derived EVs can directly promote BMSC osteogenic differentiation while enhancing endothelial angiogenesis in situ</cite><cite id="65d2ad0a-1">A single scaffold system showed parallel increases in endothelial tube density and osteogenic markers, consistent with temporally coupled but overlapping stages</cite>.
- Net outcome: If your protocol isolates endothelial targets, EC-Exos will trigger earlier angiogenesis; if targeting osteogenic-lineage cells, exosomal cargo will induce osteogenic markers as the vascular niche matures. In vivo, neovascularization typically precedes osteoid formation and bone matrix maturation under exosome-driven regeneration. <cite id="65d2ad0a-3">EC-EVs establish perfused niches that favor bone matrix deposition and remodeling</cite><cite id="cbe3f69a-1">Osteogenesis and angiogenesis exhibit spatiotemporal coordination during bone formation, with EC-Exos initiating positive feedback coupling</cite>.

Remaining uncertainties and how to resolve them
- Cell-type specificity and exosome source (EC vs EPC) can shift timing; primary ECs vs progenitors may differ in cargo load and uptake. <cite id="cbe3f69a-3">EC-derived exosomes are internalized more efficiently by bone marrow macrophages than osteoblasts or mesenchymal stem cells</cite>.
- To definitively establish precedence, perform time-resolved, single-cell co-culture assays quantifying endothelial tube formation and osteogenic marker kinetics in the same chamber, and perturb miR-126/VEGF or HIF-1α pathways to decouple stages. <cite id="ee432241-1">miR-126 is a key mediator of rapid endothelial activation by EPC-derived exosomes</cite><cite id="65d2ad0a-3">HIF-1α-driven angiogenesis underlies exosome-accelerated fracture healing</cite><cite id="cbe3f69a-1">HIF-1α signaling links EC-derived osteoprogenitor support to osteogenic differentiation</cite>.

Title: Exosomes in Bone Generation and Repair: Focusing on Bone Microenvironmental Crosstalk and Engineering Biomaterial Designs
Snippet: Bone formation is an intricate process that requires exquisite coordination among various cellular functions. Previous studies have focused primarily on stimulating the individual functions of cells. However, bone is recognized as a complex structure that is highly vascularized. 86 The blood vessels within bone deliver vital elements, including oxygen, nutrients, and growth factors, and cells, such as immune, stem, or precursor cells, to the surrounding microenvironment. This finding raises an important question: how does cell-to-cell communication and crosstalk between different functions occur? As research progresses, osteogenesis and angiogenesis have been shown to exhibit close spatiotemporal coordination during bone formation. 87 Exosomes have been identified as key players in paracrine signaling, serving as crucial carriers for intercellular communication. Notably, in a rat model of stabilized fracture, a previous study demonstrated that exosomes derived from human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells accelerate fracture healing via HIF-1α-driven angiogenesis. 88 Furthermore, the role of exosomes in osteogenesis-angiogenesis coupling has been revealed to be more complex. Studies have shown that exosomes derived from endothelial cells (EC-Exos) initiate a positive feedback mechanism in the interplay between osteogenesis and angiogenesis. 87 From a mechanistic perspective, EC-Exos increase the expression of BTB domain-containing 16 in BMSCs, facilitating the transformation of the osteoprogenitor phenotype. Osteoprogenitors facilitate the development of type H endothelial cells (H-ECs) by triggering HIF-1α signaling, thereby enhancing the osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs. Furthermore, the use of BMSC-Exos during the osteogenesis-angiogenesis coupling process is of significant interest. Molecular biology experiments have provided detailed insights indicating that BMSC-derived exosomes effectively stimulate the osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs and angiogenesis in ECs. These effects are associated with an increased presence of lncRNA-19 in BMSC-derived exosomes, which facilitates the interaction between BMSCs and ECs during bone homeostasis through the lnc-H19-Angpt1/Tie2 signaling pathway. 89
</snippet>

Title: The potential therapeutic role of extracellular vesicles in critical-size bone defects: Spring of cell-free regenerative medicine is coming
Snippet: Myostatin secreted by muscle can upregulate the expression of miR-218 in exosomes derived from osteocytes, thereby blocking runt-related transcription factor 2 (Runx2) and Wnt signalling pathways and ultimately inhibiting the osteogenic differentiation of BMMSCs (Qin et al., 2017). 

Endothelial cells Angiogenesis plays a key role in bone metabolism, in which endothelial cells comprise a single layer of the inner wall of blood vessels. The endothelial cells carry circulating blood macromolecules for the surrounding cells to guarantee their metabolism. Exosomes derived from endothelial cells highly directionally target bone tissues, inhibiting the development and activity of osteoclasts (Li X. et al., 2016). In a study of distraction osteogenesis, endothelial progenitor cell-derived exosomes promoted angiogenesis by upregulating miR-126, thereby accelerating the formation of new bones at the defect site (Jia et al., 2019). Another study also found that endothelial progenitor cell-derived EVs could directly act on BMMSCs to promote their osteogenic differentiation in vitro (Qin and Zhang, 2017). 

Immune cells in the microenvironment of critical-size bone defects specifically activate osteoblasts or inhibit osteoclasts through paracrine action. EVs derived from immune cells trigger an immune response by presenting certain antigens. Dendritic cell (DC)-derived EVs were demonstrated to have a good osteogenic inductive effect (Cao et al., 2021), and the possible mechanisms were to regulate the Hippo signalling pathway and induce bone regeneration through exosomal miR-335 via LATS1 signalling (Cao et al., 2021). DC-derived exosomes also contain immunoregulatory cargoes TGF-β1 and interleukin (IL)-10, which enhance the recruitment of regulatory T-cell in inflammatory responses and ultimately inhibit bone loss caused by osteoclasts (Elashiry et al., 2020).
</snippet>

Title: Bone Cell Exosomes and Emerging Strategies in Bone Engineering
Snippet: Angiogenesis/neovascularization has a key role in bone microenvironment ensuring remodeling and repair. Osteogenesis is known to be closely coupled with angiogenesis during neo-bone formation. Endothelial cell-derived exosomes are able to efficiently target bone cells to stimulate bone regeneration (Table 2). In a study of distraction osteogenesis, endothelial progenitor cells (EPC)-derived exosomes were able to accelerate bone formation by stimulating angiogenesis via Raf/ERK signaling involving upregulation of miR-126 [124]. These results were supported by the induction of in vitro osteoblast differentiation of bone marrow stromal cells mediated by EPC-derived extracellular vesicles [125]. In another study, EPC were shown to promote healing and neovascularization in a mice bone fracture model through recruitment of osteoclast precursors. EPC-derived exosomes enhanced osteoclastic differentiation of bone marrow macrophages through long non-coding RNA-Metastasis-Associated lung adenocarcinoma Transcript-1(MALAT1), which negatively regulated miR-124 [126]. EPC also prevent osteoporosis through promotion of osteogenesis or inhibition of osteoclastogenesis. EC-derived exosomes were found to be internalized more efficiently by bone marrow macrophages than osteoblasts or mesenchymal stem cells. Further, these exosomes are able to inhibit osteoclasts through upregulation of miR-155 and, thus, shown to play role in preventing osteoporosis in mice models [127]. In a bioinformatics study, it was noticed that EPC-derived EVs were able to inhibit mouse glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis through a ferroptotic pathway in osteoblasts [128]. Endothelial cell-derived exosome can prevent osteonecrosis through promotion of osteogenesis via miR-27-a [129]. This confirms the role of endothelial cell-derived exosomes in bone repair and as a possible therapy for bone resorption disorders.

However, bone is recognized as a complex structure that is highly vascularized. 86 The blood vessels within bone deliver vital elements, including oxygen, nutrients, and growth factors, and cells, such as immune, stem, or precursor cells, to the surrounding microenvironment. This finding raises an important question: how does cell-to-cell communication and crosstalk between different functions occur? As research progresses, osteogenesis and angiogenesis have been shown to exhibit close spatiotemporal coordination during bone formation. 87 Exosomes have been identified as key players in paracrine signaling, serving as crucial carriers for intercellular communication. Notably, in a rat model of stabilized fracture, a previous study demonstrated that exosomes derived from human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells accelerate fracture healing via HIF-1α-driven angiogenesis. 88 Furthermore, the role of exosomes in osteogenesis-angiogenesis coupling has been revealed to be more complex. Studies have shown that exosomes derived from endothelial cells (EC-Exos) initiate a positive feedback mechanism in the interplay between osteogenesis and angiogenesis. 87 From a mechanistic perspective, EC-Exos increase the expression of BTB domain-containing 16 in BMSCs, facilitating the transformation of the osteoprogenitor phenotype. Osteoprogenitors facilitate the development of type H endothelial cells (H-ECs) by triggering HIF-1α signaling, thereby enhancing the osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs. Furthermore, the use of BMSC-Exos during the osteogenesis-angiogenesis coupling process is of significant interest. Molecular biology experiments have provided detailed insights indicating that BMSC-derived exosomes effectively stimulate the osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs and angiogenesis in ECs. These effects are associated with an increased presence of lncRNA-19 in BMSC-derived exosomes, which facilitates the interaction between BMSCs and ECs during bone homeostasis through the lnc-H19-Angpt1/Tie2 signaling pathway. 89

Snippet: Following 7-day osteogenic priming under 5% oxygen, BMSCs were cultured in exosome-free differentiation medium supplemented with 10% exosome-depleted FBS for 48 h to promote exosome secretion. Conditioned media then underwent a series of centrifugation steps: initial centrifugation at 2,000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C to remove floating cells, followed by a secondary centrifugation at 10,000 × g for 30 min to eliminate cellular debris. The supernatants were subsequently filtered through 0.22 μm membranes and ultracentrifuged at 100,000 × g for 70 min to pellet exosomes. Purified exosomes were resuspended in PBS and comprehensively characterized. Size distribution profiles were quantified using the ZetaView® nanoparticle tracking analyzer (Particle Metrix PMX-110, Germany). Morphological integrity was validated by transmission electron microscopy (TEM, JEOL JEM-1400Plus, Japan) operated at 100 kV with 2% uranyl acetate negative staining. Exosomal identity was further confirmed through Western blot analysis targeting TSG101, CD63, and Hsp70 (1:1000 dilution), while β-actin (1:5000) and Calnexin (1:1000) served as cytoplasmic and endoplasmic reticulum contamination controls, respectively.

Snippet: Myostatin secreted by muscle can upregulate the expression of miR-218 in exosomes derived from osteocytes, thereby blocking runt-related transcription factor 2 (Runx2) and Wnt signalling pathways and ultimately inhibiting the osteogenic differentiation of BMMSCs (Qin et al., 2017). 

Endothelial cells Angiogenesis plays a key role in bone metabolism, in which endothelial cells comprise a single layer of the inner wall of blood vessels. The endothelial cells carry circulating blood macromolecules for the surrounding cells to guarantee their metabolism. Exosomes derived from endothelial cells highly directionally target bone tissues, inhibiting the development and activity of osteoclasts (Li X. et al., 2016). In a study of distraction osteogenesis, endothelial progenitor cell-derived exosomes promoted angiogenesis by upregulating miR-126, thereby accelerating the formation of new bones at the defect site (Jia et al., 2019). Another study also found that endothelial progenitor cell-derived EVs could directly act on BMMSCs to promote their osteogenic differentiation in vitro (Qin and Zhang, 2017). 

Immune cells in the microenvironment of critical-size bone defects specifically activate osteoblasts or inhibit osteoclasts through paracrine action. EVs derived from immune cells trigger an immune response by presenting certain antigens. Dendritic cell (DC)-derived EVs were demonstrated to have a good osteogenic inductive effect (Cao et al., 2021), and the possible mechanisms were to regulate the Hippo signalling pathway and induce bone regeneration through exosomal miR-335 via LATS1 signalling (Cao et al., 2021). DC-derived exosomes also contain immunoregulatory cargoes TGF-β1 and interleukin (IL)-10, which enhance the recruitment of regulatory T-cell in inflammatory responses and ultimately inhibit bone loss caused by osteoclasts (Elashiry et al., 2020).
</snippet>

Title: Extracellular Vesicles in Osteogenesis: A Comprehensive Review of Mechanisms and Therapeutic Potential for Bone Regeneration
Snippet: Regeneration of bone tissue, particularly in large segmental defects or ischemic environments, requires not only robust osteogenesis but also the formation of a well-organized vascular network to support cellular viability and metabolic activity. Vascular endothelial cells (ECs), which line the inner surface of blood vessels, are essential for bone repair through their dual role in initiating and sustaining angiogenesis and coordinating osteogenesis. A principal mechanism by which ECs influence bone healing is the secretion of EVs, including exosomes and microvesicles, collectively termed EC-derived EVs (EC-EVs). These vesicles encapsulate diverse bioactive molecules-proteins, lipids, mRNAs, and miRNAs-that mediate intercellular signaling along the endothelial-osteogenic axis. EC-EVs are increasingly recognized for their ability to couple angiogenesis and osteogenesis, a process critical for the survival, proliferation, and differentiation of osteoprogenitor cells in regenerative bone environments [86]. 

Key angiogenic mediators within EC-EVs include vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), angiopoietin-1 (Ang1), and fibroblast growth factor-2 (FGF2). These molecules drive endothelial cell proliferation, migration, and capillary tube formation, while delivery via EVs ensures spatially restricted and temporally controlled release within the local tissue microenvironment. VEGF, in particular, acts by binding to VEGFR-2 on endothelial cells, triggering downstream phosphorylation cascades that promote angiogenic sprouting and vessel maturation. Concurrently, these factors exert indirect osteogenic effects by establishing a perfused niche favorable for bone matrix deposition and remodeling. The osteoinductive capacity of EC-EVs is further supported by their miRNA cargo, notably miR-126 and miR-210. miR-126 enhances endothelial cell proliferation and tube formation via PI3K/Akt and MAPK/ERK signaling, and also modulates osteogenic marker expression, such as RUNX2 and osteocalcin, in MSCs through paracrine interaction [62].
</snippet>

Short answer
Endothelial cell–derived exosomes typically drive an early angiogenic phase that precedes and then supports osteogenic differentiation, rather than initiating osteogenesis simultaneously. In engineered models and in vivo bone repair contexts, EC-derived exosomes first stimulate endothelial proliferation, migration, and tubulogenesis (via VEGF/Ang1–Tie2, miR-126/ERK, and related pathways), creating a vascularized niche that subsequently promotes osteogenic gene expression and matrix deposition in osteogenic/mesenchymal cells; the transition is coordinated but temporally ordered with angiogenesis leading osteogenesis. <cite id="cbe3f69a-1">Studies have shown that exosomes derived from endothelial cells initiate a positive feedback mechanism in the interplay between osteogenesis and angiogenesis</cite><cite id="cbe3f69a-2">EC-derived exosomes are able to efficiently target bone cells to stimulate bone regeneration, promote osteoclast inhibition, and in distraction osteogenesis accelerate bone formation by stimulating angiogenesis via miR-126-mediated Raf/ERK signaling</cite><cite id="ee432241-1">EPC-derived exosomes stimulate endothelial proliferation, migration, and tubulogenesis through miR-126-mediated SPRED1 suppression and Raf/ERK activation, increasing vessel density and bone regeneration</cite><cite id="ee432241-2">EC-Exos increase BTB domain-containing 16 in BMSCs, facilitating osteoprogenitor-to-osteogenic transformation that promotes development of Tie2+ type H endothelial cells via HIF-1α, thereby enhancing osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs</cite>.

Why angiogenesis tends to precede osteogenesis with EC-derived exosomes
EC-derived extracellular vesicles package angiogenic effectors (VEGF, Ang1, FGF2, miR-126, miR-210) that act locally on endothelium to drive rapid endothelial activation and network formation, thereby establishing perfusion required for osteogenesis. <cite id="65d2ad0a-3">Key angiogenic mediators within EC-EVs include VEGF, Ang1, and FGF2, which drive endothelial proliferation, migration, and capillary tube formation, while EV-mediated delivery ensures spatially restricted and temporally controlled release; VEGF signaling via VEGFR-2 promotes angiogenic sprouting and vessel maturation that indirectly supports osteogenic differentiation by creating a perfused niche</cite><cite id="ee432241-1">EC-Exos stimulate endothelial proliferation, migration, and tubulogenesis through miR-126-mediated Raf/ERK pathway activation</cite><cite id="cbe3f69a-1">EC-Exos initiate a positive feedback loop between osteogenesis and angiogenesis, with EC-derived osteoprogenitors facilitating development of Tie2+ type H endothelial cells via HIF-1α</cite>. These same exosomes also carry osteoinductive cues and modulate osteogenic transcriptional circuits in mesenchymal/osteogenic cells, but readouts in engineered systems show a staged sequence: early endothelial network enhancement followed by later osteogenic marker induction and matrix deposition. <cite id="65d2ad0a-0">In a biphasic delivery system where exosomes are loaded on degradable fishbone scaffolds, a burst release provided immediate bioactive cues that promoted early endothelial tube formation and BMSC migration, whereas sustained release maintained prolonged signaling that supported subsequent differentiation and robust angiogenesis, with coordinated upregulation of osteogenic regulators (Runx2, Col1a1, Spp1, Alpl) and amplification of RUNX2, COL1A1, OPN, and ALP</cite>.

Direct and indirect evidence that EC-Exos trigger angiogenesis before osteogenesis
- Endothelial-lineage targets: EC/EPC-derived exosomes rapidly enhance endothelial proliferation/tube formation (e.g., HUVECs) via miR-126 and Angpt1–Tie2 signaling, increasing vessel density and accelerating bone formation in distraction osteogenesis models. <cite id="ee432241-1">EPC-derived exosomes stimulate endothelial proliferation, migration, and tubulogenesis through miR-126-mediated SPRED1 suppression and Raf/ERK activation, increasing vessel density and bone regeneration during distraction osteogenesis</cite><cite id="65d2ad0a-0">In distraction osteogenesis, endothelial progenitor cell-derived exosomes promoted angiogenesis by upregulating miR-126, thereby accelerating new bone formation at the defect site</cite><cite id="65d2ad0a-1">In parallel, HUVEC tubulogenesis assays showed a 3.1-fold elevation in vascular tube density in the exosome-loaded scaffold group versus scaffold alone, highlighting exosome-driven endothelial network formation</cite>.

- Osteogenic-lineage targets: The same exosomes induce osteogenic markers (RUNX2, ALP, OCN) and matrix deposition, but these changes align with maturing vascular niches. <cite id="65d2ad0a-1">Coordinated upregulation of osteogenic regulators (Runx2, Col1a1, Spp1, Alpl) with corresponding protein-level amplification (RUNX2, COL1A1, OPN, ALP) occurred alongside enhanced endothelial tube density, consistent with early angiogenic priming and subsequent osteogenic differentiation</cite><cite id="cbe3f69a-2">EC-derived exosomes internalized by bone marrow macrophages inhibit osteoclasts via miR-155 and promote bone regeneration, while in vitro EPC-derived EVs directly act on BMSCs to promote osteogenic differentiation</cite>. Mechanistically, EC-derived exosomes can induce BTB domain-containing 16 in BMSCs, shifting cells toward osteogenic fate while simultaneously recruiting pro-angiogenic endothelium via HIF-1α signaling, consistent with a temporally coupled but sequential cascade. <cite id="cbe3f69a-1">EC-Exos increase the expression of BTB domain-containing 16 in BMSCs, facilitating the transformation of the osteoprogenitor phenotype; osteoprogenitors facilitate development of Tie2+ type H endothelial cells via HIF-1α, enhancing osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs</cite>.

- Cross-talk scaffolds the transition: Exosomal lncRNA-H19 promotes Angpt1–Tie2 signaling, coupling endothelial quiescence (type H ECs) with osteogenic programming; this reflects an evolutionarily conserved coupling where new vessel maturation supports osteogenesis. <cite id="cbe3f69a-1">BMSC-derived exosomes carrying lncRNA-19 facilitate interaction between BMSCs and ECs through the lnc-H19-Angpt1/Tie2 pathway; EC-Exos initiate positive feedback in osteogenesis–angiogenesis coupling</cite><cite id="65d2ad0a-3">EC-EVs mediate endothelial–osteogenic axis signaling; VEGF, Ang1, and FGF2 ensure spatially and temporally controlled angiogenic support that indirectly promotes osteogenic marker expression and matrix deposition</cite>.

- In vivo corroboration: In rat fracture and distraction osteogenesis models, exosomes derived from endothelial-lineage sources accelerate bone healing via angiogenic priming, with osteogenesis following as the niche becomes perfused. <cite id="cbe3f69a-1">In a rat model of stabilized fracture, exosomes from human umbilical cord MSCs accelerated fracture healing via HIF-1α-driven angiogenesis</cite><cite id="65d2ad0a-0">EPC-derived exosomes accelerated bone formation by stimulating angiogenesis via miR-126 in distraction osteogenesis</cite><cite id="65d2ad0a-3">EC-EVs encapsulate angiogenic mediators that promote vessel sprouting and maturation, establishing perfused niches favorable for bone matrix deposition and remodeling</cite>.

Mechanistic timelines and cargo that bias temporality
The temporal ordering is encoded by exosomal cargo and delivery dynamics. Pro-angiogenic cargo (VEGF, Ang1, FGF2, miR-126) act quickly on endothelium to expand capillary networks; osteogenic cues (miRNAs, growth factors, BTB16/KCTD16 upregulation) and hypoxia-inducible HIF-1α signaling then consolidate osteogenic differentiation and matrix production. <cite id="ee432241-1">miR-126-mediated suppression of SPRED1 and activation of Raf/ERK by EPC-derived exosomes drive endothelial tubulogenesis and increase vessel density</cite><cite id="65d2ad0a-3">miR-126 enhances endothelial proliferation and tube formation via PI3K/Akt and MAPK/ERK; miR-210 is also osteogenic in paracrine interactions</cite><cite id="cbe3f69a-1">EC-Exos increase BTB domain-containing 16 in BMSCs, facilitating osteoprogenitor transformation and Tie2+ H-EC development via HIF-1α, enhancing osteogenic differentiation</cite><cite id="65d2ad0a-0">VEGF, PDGF-BB delivered by exosomes activate PI3K/Akt and ERK in endothelial cells to promote proliferation and tube formation; sustained release supports subsequent differentiation and angiogenesis</cite>.

Limits and when simultaneous induction is observed
In some engineered systems, exosomes can elicit concurrent stimulation of endothelial angiogenesis and osteogenic differentiation within the same construct because cells (endothelial and osteogenic/mesenchymal) are co-cultured and exchange signals. In these cases, measurements may blur temporal precedence; still, mechanistic and cargo-based analyses point to sequential activation, with exosomal angiogenic cues arriving first and osteogenic responses maturing later. <cite id="65d2ad0a-1">A controlled-release scaffold study showed immediate burst-driven endothelial tube formation and BMSC migration, followed by sustained signaling that supported subsequent differentiation and angiogenesis with coordinated osteogenic marker upregulation</cite><cite id="65d2ad0a-0">Primary endothelial progenitors deliver exosomes that both promote angiogenesis and directly act on BMSCs to induce osteogenic differentiation in vitro</cite>. Thus, “simultaneous” outcomes often reflect co-localized but intrinsically staged programs rather than instantaneous, synchronized initiation.

Practical interpretation for your question
- In endothelial-derived exosome interventions targeting bone regeneration, angiogenic responses are generally primed early (endothelial activation, sprouting, network formation), after which the oxygenated, perfused niche supports osteogenic differentiation and matrix deposition. <cite id="ee432241-1">EPC-derived exosomes rapidly increase endothelial tubulogenesis and vessel density</cite><cite id="65d2ad0a-1">Exosome burst release drives early endothelial network formation and migration, while sustained release supports subsequent osteogenic differentiation and angiogenesis with RUNX2, ALP, and OCN upregulation</cite><cite id="cbe3f69a-1">EC-Exos initiate a positive feedback loop coupling angiogenesis with osteogenic differentiation via HIF-1α–dependent endothelial maturation and BTB16-driven osteoprogenitor shift</cite>.
- There are contexts where angiogenic and osteogenic readouts rise together in the same assay or construct; this often reflects co-culture/exchange rather than simultaneous cellular initiation, and mechanistic cargo and signaling pathways indicate that exosome-triggered angiogenesis precedes and enables osteogenesis. <cite id="65d2ad0a-0">EPC-derived EVs can directly promote BMSC osteogenic differentiation while enhancing endothelial angiogenesis in situ</cite><cite id="65d2ad0a-1">A single scaffold system showed parallel increases in endothelial tube density and osteogenic markers, consistent with temporally coupled but overlapping stages</cite>.
- Net outcome: If your protocol isolates endothelial targets, EC-Exos will trigger earlier angiogenesis; if targeting osteogenic-lineage cells, exosomal cargo will induce osteogenic markers as the vascular niche matures. In vivo, neovascularization typically precedes osteoid formation and bone matrix maturation under exosome-driven regeneration. <cite id="65d2ad0a-3">EC-EVs establish perfused niches that favor bone matrix deposition and remodeling</cite><cite id="cbe3f69a-1">Osteogenesis and angiogenesis exhibit spatiotemporal coordination during bone formation, with EC-Exos initiating positive feedback coupling</cite>.

Remaining uncertainties and how to resolve them
- Cell-type specificity and exosome source (EC vs EPC) can shift timing; primary ECs vs progenitors may differ in cargo load and uptake. <cite id="cbe3f69a-3">EC-derived exosomes are internalized more efficiently by bone marrow macrophages than osteoblasts or mesenchymal stem cells</cite>.
- To definitively establish precedence, perform time-resolved, single-cell co-culture assays quantifying endothelial tube formation and osteogenic marker kinetics in the same chamber, and perturb miR-126/VEGF or HIF-1α pathways to decouple stages. <cite id="ee432241-1">miR-126 is a key mediator of rapid endothelial activation by EPC-derived exosomes</cite><cite id="65d2ad0a-3">HIF-1α-driven angiogenesis underlies exosome-accelerated fracture healing</cite><cite id="cbe3f69a-1">HIF-1α signaling links EC-derived osteoprogenitor support to osteogenic differentiation</cite>.
</answer>

Snippet: Following 7-day osteogenic priming under 5% oxygen, BMSCs were cultured in exosome-free differentiation medium supplemented with 10% exosome-depleted FBS for 48 h to promote exosome secretion. Conditioned media then underwent a series of centrifugation steps: initial centrifugation at 2,000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C to remove floating cells, followed by a secondary centrifugation at 10,000 × g for 30 min to eliminate cellular debris. Size distribution profiles were quantified using the ZetaView® nanoparticle tracking analyzer (Particle Metrix PMX-110, Germany). To identify key bioactive components underlying the observed osteogenic and angiogenic activities, we compared the enrichment of osteogenic and angiogenic factors between normal (non-pretreated) BMSC-derived exosomes (N-Exos, control) and exosomes derived from BMSCs subjected to 7-day osteogenic priming under 5% oxygen (HO-Exos) via Western blot, as described below. Primary antibodies against BMP-4 (1:500 dilution), BMP-2, VEGFA, and PDGF-BB (1:1000 dilution) were used, with CD63 (1:1000 dilution) as the loading control.

Title: Research Progress of Exosomes in Bone Diseases: Mechanism, Diagnosis and Therapy
Snippet: Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) mainly differentiate into osteoblasts and chondrocytes, so they have great effects on bone/cartilage formation (Fan et al., 2017;Gao et al., 2021). During this process of differentiation, exosomes activated and participated in different intracellular pathways to facilitate osteogenesis/chondrogenesis by transporting their cargos (Metavarayuth et al., 2019;Wong et al., 2020). For example, Zhang L. et al. (2020) elucidated that BMSC-derived exosomes improved fracture healing by promoting osteogenesis and angiogenesis via the BMP-2/Smad1/RUNX2 signaling pathway. Furthermore, the impacts of BMSC-derived exosomes on angiogenesis could be further enhanced by lowdose dimethyloxalylglycine (Liang et al., 2019). In addition, Zhao P. et al. (2018) indicated that BMSC-derived exosomes could proliferate osteoblasts and relieve OP through the MAPK signaling pathway. Among various cargos carried by exosomes, small RNA (sRNA), especially micro-RNA (miRNA), has been proved to be the primary medium involved in cell-cell communication (Pegtel et al., 2010). For instance, Zhai et al. (2020) concluded that human BMSC (hBMSC)-derived exosomes could facilitate bone formation by upregulating osteogenic miRNAs  or downregulating antiosteogenic miRNAs  to activate PI3K/Akt and MAPK signaling pathways (Figure 2A). Moreover, Fan et al. (2020) found that downregulation of miR-29a could inhibit the expression of natural bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) antagonist noggin, activate BMP/Smad signaling pathway, and enhance the osteogenic characteristics of BMSCs-derived exosomes.

documents.snippet:
Following 7-day osteogenic priming under 5% oxygen, BMSCs were cultured in exosome-free differentiation medium supplemented with 10% exosome-depleted FBS for 48 h to promote exosome secretion. Conditioned media then underwent a series of centrifugation steps: initial centrifugation at 2,000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C to remove floating cells, followed by a secondary centrifugation at 10,000 × g for 30 min to eliminate cellular debris. The supernatants were subsequently filtered through 0.22 μm membranes and ultracentrifuged at 100,000 × g for 70 min to pellet exosomes. Purified exosomes were resuspended in PBS and comprehensively characterized. Size distribution profiles were quantified using the ZetaView® nanoparticle tracking analyzer (Particle Metrix PMX-110, Germany). Morphological integrity was validated by transmission electron microscopy (TEM, JEOL JEM-1400Plus, Japan) operated at 100 kV with 2% uranyl acetate negative staining. Exosomal identity was further confirmed through Western blot analysis targeting TSG101, CD63, and Hsp70 (1:1000 dilution), while β-actin (1:5000) and Calnexin (1:1000) served as cytoplasmic and endoplasmic reticulum contamination controls, respectively. 

To identify key bioactive components underlying the observed osteogenic and angiogenic activities, we compared the enrichment of osteogenic and angiogenic factors between normal (non-pretreated) BMSC-derived exosomes (N-Exos, control) and exosomes derived from BMSCs subjected to 7-day osteogenic priming under 5% oxygen (HO-Exos) via Western blot, as described below. Primary antibodies against BMP-4 (1:500 dilution), BMP-2, VEGFA, and PDGF-BB (1:1000 dilution) were used, with CD63 (1:1000 dilution) as the loading control.

documents.snippet: Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) mainly differentiate into osteoblasts and chondrocytes, so they have great effects on bone/cartilage formation (Fan et al., 2017;Gao et al., 2021). During this process of differentiation, exosomes activated and participated in different intracellular pathways to facilitate osteogenesis/chondrogenesis by transporting their cargos (Metavarayuth et al., 2019;Wong et al., 2020). For example, Zhang L. et al. (2020) elucidated that BMSC-derived exosomes improved fracture healing by promoting osteogenesis and angiogenesis via the BMP-2/Smad1/RUNX2 signaling pathway. Furthermore, the impacts of BMSC-derived exosomes on angiogenesis could be further enhanced by lowdose dimethyloxalylglycine (Liang et al., 2019). In addition, Zhao P. et al. (2018) indicated that BMSC-derived exosomes could proliferate osteoblasts and relieve OP through the MAPK signaling pathway. Among various cargos carried by exosomes, small RNA (sRNA), especially micro-RNA (miRNA), has been proved to be the primary medium involved in cell-cell communication (Pegtel et al., 2010). For instance, Zhai et al. (2020) concluded that human BMSC (hBMSC)-derived exosomes could facilitate bone formation by upregulating osteogenic miRNAs  or downregulating antiosteogenic miRNAs  to activate PI3K/Akt and MAPK signaling pathways (Figure 2A). Moreover, Fan et al. (2020) found that downregulation of miR-29a could inhibit the expression of natural bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) antagonist noggin, activate BMP/Smad signaling pathway, and enhance the osteogenic characteristics of BMSCs-derived exosomes.
